nodes.title: Compact assembly of seminormed rings
nodes.statement: The category of commutative unital seminormed rings and contractive maps has filtered colimits commuting with finite limits and is generated under colimits by objects admitting a sequential presentation along weakly compact maps; hence it is compactly assembled. A map f:X→Y is weakly compact when every Y→colim_i Z_i factors after composition with f through some Z_i. This assertion is not made for complete Banach rings.
hypotheses: Seminorms may vanish identically; the zero ring is allowed.
Use the nonstable definition of compact assembly and a fixed universe.
proofSteps: Import the nonstable compact-assembly criterion requested from E5. Express a free generator of radius r as the colimit of radii r′>r; contraction of radii gives weakly compact transition maps.

Present arbitrary seminormed rings by free rings and impose relations by finite limits/colimits; verify filtered colimits commute with the finite limits in this category. Completion is a separate functor, so the argument does not assert compact assembly after completion.

sources.match: The radius-shrinking presentation supplies compact assembly in the seminormed category.

acceptance: Verify the lifting condition is imposed on the composite from X, not on Y.
The Banach completion functor must not be used to transfer the conclusion without proof.
Check generation under colimits by sequential weakly compact presentations; do not require every object itself to have such a presentation.

nodes.title: Banach arc-topology
nodes.statement: On the opposite category of Banach rings, a family {A→B_i} covers exactly when a finite subfamily induces a surjection ⨿ M(B_i)→M(A). Let Marc(A) be the arc-sheafification of its representable presheaf. A small arc-stack is a sheaf of spaces admitting a presentation as a small colimit of these representables at some uncountable regular cardinal cutoff κ; identify the compatible enlargements of κ.
hypotheses: All ring morphisms are contractive and completed tensor products are the categorical pushouts.
Choose a universe and a regular uncountable κ large enough for the presentation.
proofSteps: Use TB spectra of pushouts to show pullback stability of finite spectral surjectivity, and compose finite covers.

Apply the existing GrothendieckTopology carrier to the generated sieves, and the requested enhanced sheaf machinery to sheafify representables. Show the change-of-cutoff functors agree on κ-small objects.

sources.match: Finite jointly surjective spectra define the site; representables need sheafification.

acceptance: Prove equivalence with lifting a geometric Banach-field point after a field extension.
Do not identify Marc(A)(B) with contractive ring maps on the entire site.

nodes.title: Uniformization and geometric arc-covers
nodes.statement: Analytic covers are arc-covers. Uniform completion induces Marc(A)≃Marc(A^u). The product of completed residue fields is an arc-cover. In characteristic p, the norm-corrected perfection is arc-equivalent. Over the complex numbers, the Gelfand transform identifies Marc(A) with the compact-Hausdorff space M(A) viewed as a condensed sheaf; over the reals retain complex conjugation.
hypotheses: Use uniform completion and rescaled norms in perfection, not an algebraic perfection with arbitrary norm.
The residue-field product uses bounded families with its product norm.
proofSteps: Check the geometric-field lifting criterion for each construction using the imported residue-field and Gelfand theorems.
Use spectral-radius equality to identify geometric maps through uniformization. For real rings descend the complex description with its involution.

sources.match: The main examples explain what geometry the arc-sheafification retains.

acceptance: The real case retains its involution.
The product of residue fields is not asserted to have algebraically closed residues.

nodes.title: Strictly totally disconnected Banach rings
nodes.statement: A Banach ring A is strictly totally disconnected if it is analytic and uniform, M(A) is profinite, and each completed residue field is algebraically closed. Its associated arc-sheaf is the corresponding strictly totally disconnected affine object.
hypotheses: Analytic means that a finite family of topologically nilpotent elements generates the unit ideal.
proofSteps: Combine the imported analytic/uniform predicates with the profinite spectrum and algebraically closed completed residue fields.
Keep the residue-field condition as part of the structure exposed by the API; a totally disconnected spectrum alone is insufficient.

sources.match: Strict disconnectedness includes residue algebraic closure, analyticity and uniformity.

acceptance: Identify clopen restrictions and finite products with the same predicates.

api.name: strict_clopen
api.statement: Restriction to a clopen spectral subset is strictly totally disconnected.

api.name: strict_residue
api.statement: At every spectral point the completed residue field is algebraically closed.

api.name: strict_products
api.statement: Finite products and the bounded product of nondiscrete algebraically closed Banach fields are strictly totally disconnected.

tests.name: field
tests.statement: A nondiscrete complete algebraically closed valued field is strictly totally disconnected.

tests.name: real_field

tests.name: ultrafilters
tests.statement: For an infinite bounded product of such fields the spectrum is βI, and includes nonprincipal ultrafilters; it is not the discrete set I.

uses.how: The finitary condition is tested on this basis.
Free-motive evaluation and cancellation reduce to this basis.

nodes.title: Strict basis and restricted subcanonicity
nodes.statement: Every Banach ring has an arc-cover by a strictly totally disconnected ring. The arc-topology is subcanonical on the full strictly totally disconnected subcategory, and on perfectoid rings with |p|<1. This is restricted subcanonicity, not subcanonicity of the entire Banach site.
hypotheses: In the perfectoid assertion p is a prime and the perfectoid norm convention is the imported one.
proofSteps: Choose algebraic closures of completed residue fields and use their bounded product to obtain the cover. Use the Banach-ultraproduct description to check all new residues are algebraically closed.
For strict rings reconstruct sections using profinite clopens; for perfectoids use the v-descent theorem imported from DiamondsAndVStacks.

sources.match: The strict basis covers the site and has effective representable descent.

acceptance: Check the infinite product includes its ultraproduct points.
A proof may not replace arc-sheafification globally by Yoneda.

nodes.title: Quasi-pro-étale Banach maps
nodes.statement: A map A→B is quasi-pro-étale if for each geometric point A→C with C nondiscrete algebraically closed, the uniform completion of B⊗̂_A C is Cont(S,C) for a profinite set S. If both A and B are strictly totally disconnected, such maps A→B identify with profinite sets over M(A).
hypotheses: Base change includes uniform completion; use continuous C-valued functions with the supremum norm.
proofSteps: For both source and target strictly totally disconnected, use the strict-basis description and clopen gluing to construct the profinite-set equivalence.
Check the condition pointwise and prove stability under completed base change and composition.

sources.match: The geometric fibre condition is profinite continuous functions, not finite étaleness.

acceptance: Show analytic covers of strict bases are quasi-pro-étale.

api.name: qproet_base_change
api.statement: Quasi-pro-étale maps are stable under base change and composition.

api.name: qproet_strict_equivalence
api.statement: For A strictly totally disconnected, the category of quasi-pro-étale A-algebras B that are also strictly totally disconnected is equivalent to profinite sets over M(A).

api.name: qproet_clopen
api.statement: Clopen restrictions are quasi-pro-étale.

tests.statement: The identity corresponds to a one-point fibre.

tests.name: profinite_fibre
tests.statement: For C nondiscrete algebraically closed and an infinite profinite S, Cont(S,C) is strictly totally disconnected and quasi-pro-étale over C, but need not be finite étale over C.

tests.name: ball_nonexample

uses.how: Gives the scope of the finitary projection formula.
Supplies the proper maps used for module-category descent.

nodes.title: Repleteness of the arc-topos
nodes.statement: In the Banach arc-topos, inverse limits of countable towers of epimorphisms remain epimorphic. Consequently its hypercomplete space-valued sheaves are Postnikov complete by the requested Mondal–Reinecke theorem; do not infer the consequence solely from the abelian derived repleteness theorem.
hypotheses: Countable inverse systems; preserve the chosen cardinal cutoff by enlargement when necessary.
proofSteps: On geometric field points lift a countable tower of covers successively to field extensions, and complete the directed union. The resulting extension provides a simultaneous lift.
Use the finite-subfamily criterion to promote local lifts to epimorphisms of sheaves. Apply precisely the general replete hypercomplete infinity-topos Postnikov theorem requested from E2.

sources.locator: §4, proof of Theorem 4.20, p. 24; §3, geometric-point cover criterion, pp. 14–15
sources.match: Proper base change uses repleteness of this site and the general Postnikov theorem.

acceptance: Distinguish countable repleteness from a claim that all limits preserve epimorphisms.
Record the E2 space-valued hypothesis; its existing derived-category statement alone is insufficient.

nodes.title: Finitary strict-basis hypersheaf theorem
nodes.statement: Any space-valued functor on strictly totally disconnected Banach rings which preserves finite products and filtered colimits extends uniquely to a hypercomplete arc-sheaf. For abelian-group-valued such functors positive cohomology vanishes on strict bases. The same criterion applies to compactly assembled target categories with the required finite-limit compatibility.
hypotheses: The colimits of rings are completed filtered colimits.
For the generalized target use the exact compact-assembly hypotheses, not just presentability.
proofSteps: Extend n-truncated functors along quasi-pro-étale maps; Lemma 4.7 gives filtered continuity of this extension.

Prove the splitting lemma: an arc-cover of a strict base is a completed filtered colimit of split maps. Use seminormed compact assembly to reduce to finitely many approximate relations; a surjective open subset of affine space has a section by algebraic closure and clopen patching.
For each n commute the finite descent limit through the filtered colimit of split maps, then pass to the Postnikov limit. The abelian assertion follows from the same computation.

sources.match: Filtered split approximation and finite truncations establish hyperdescent.

acceptance: Check that the infinite totalization is handled after truncation, not exchanged with a filtered colimit without a bound.

nodes.title: Finitary derived arc-sheaves
nodes.statement: Dfin(X,Z) is the full stable infinity-subcategory of derived hypercomplete abelian arc-sheaves whose restriction to strictly totally disconnected Banach rings over X commutes with filtered colimits. It is equivalently the category of finite-product- and filtered-colimit-preserving functors from this basis to D(Z).
hypotheses: X is a small arc-stack.
Use the enhanced derived category, rather than only its homotopy category.
proofSteps: Apply the strict-basis hypersheaf criterion degreewise/enhanced to construct the restriction equivalence.
Compute colimits and truncations on the strict basis; this proves stability under both and left completeness. Tensor and pullback are the inherited derived operations.

sources.match: Finitarity is imposed on the strict basis to control unbounded Postnikov limits.

acceptance: For bounded-below objects extend continuity to all Banach rings. For unbounded objects require a uniform cohomological-dimension bound to make that extension.

api.name: dfin_restriction
api.statement: Restriction gives the stated basis-functor equivalence.

api.name: dfin_pullback_tensor
api.statement: Derived pullbacks are symmetric monoidal and compose coherently.

api.name: dfin_truncations
api.statement: The full subcategory is stable under colimits and truncations and is left complete.

tests.name: strict_value
tests.statement: At a strict base positive cohomology of a degree-zero finitary sheaf vanishes.

tests.name: bounded_continuity
tests.statement: A bounded-below finitary object commutes with filtered colimits of arbitrary Banach algebras.

tests.name: complex_point

Its spectral counterpart hosts motivic K-theory.

nodes.title: Complex and geometric-point comparison
nodes.statement: For a complex Banach algebra A, Dfin(Marc(A),Z) is the left-completed derived category of sheaves on the compact Hausdorff space M(A). For every finitary object M, a nondiscrete Banach field K and completed algebraic closure C, M(K)≃M(C)^{hG_K}, with continuous Galois action. For M bounded below, the stalk at x of Rν_*M on M(A) equals M(K(x)).
hypotheses: The Galois action uses continuous discrete modules inside the condensed/profinite action category.
The stalk formula is stated for bounded-below finitary objects.
proofSteps: On strict complex bases identify the arc-site with profinite sets over M(A); finitary objects become ordinary sheaves, then descend.
Use the profinite Galois site to compute values at a Banach field. Extend bounded-below continuity to identify neighbourhood germs with the completed residue field.

sources.match: Complex sheaves and continuous Galois cohomology give two computations of finitary objects.

acceptance: Retain left completion.
Over the complex point the category is D(Z); do not infer all complex-base effective motives equal all finitary sheaves.

nodes.title: Proper maps and cohomological dimension
nodes.statement: For a small arc-stack X, d(X) is the cohomological dimension of global sections on Dfin(X,Z), measured on degree-zero objects. A 0-truncated map f:Y→X is proper if it is qcqs. Define d(f)=sup_x d(Y_x) over geometric points x; locally finite dimension means finite dimension after pullback to each quasicompact substack of X.
hypotheses: Dimension may be infinite; a finite bound is additional data for the theorems using it.
proofSteps: Use the derived global-sections functor to define the vanishing bound. Define relative dimension by geometric fibres and use the strict basis to compare base changes.
Combine the stalk formula with the spectral sequence on M(A): for analytic A, d(Marc(A)) is at most cd(M(A))+sup_x cd(G_K(x)).

sources.match: Proper here is a sheaf-theoretic qcqs condition on 0-truncated maps; dimension is cohomological.

acceptance: Keep topological cohomological dimension separate from covering dimension unless the required comparison theorem is supplied.

api.name: dimension_bound
api.statement: The analytic spectral-space plus residue-Galois bound holds with the stated suprema.

api.name: proper_base_change
api.statement: Properness is preserved by base change.

api.name: dimension_local
api.statement: Local finite dimension can be checked on quasicompact target charts.

tests.name: strict_zero
tests.statement: A strict affine base has d=0 for finitary degree-zero sheaves.

tests.name: profinite_fibre

tests.name: truncation_guard
tests.statement: The map B(C₂)→* for the constant cyclic group of order two is not 0-truncated, and hence is not proper in this sense.

Controls pushforwards and the scope of rigidity.

nodes.title: Proper base change for finitary sheaves
nodes.statement: For a 0-truncated proper map f:Y→X of small arc-sheaves with finite d(f), Rf_* preserves Dfin, has the fibrewise cohomological bound, and commutes with every base change on Dfin. If f is quasi-pro-étale it also satisfies the projection formula. No general proper projection formula is asserted at this stage.
hypotheses: In the bounded-below preservation argument finite d(f) is unnecessary; the unbounded conclusion uses it.
proofSteps: Resolve the qcqs source by affine charts and prove bounded-below finitary preservation using all-Banach continuity.
Use repleteness and the requested space-valued Postnikov theorem plus finite d(f) to pass to unbounded objects. Base change is computed by slices and geometric fibres.
For quasi-pro-étale f write each fibre as an inverse limit of finite sets; finite-set projection and finitarity give the projection formula.

sources.match: Proper base change holds before stabilization but projection has an extra restriction.

acceptance: Reproduce the failure for P¹→* using the reduced multiplicative group once BM.3 is available.
Verify base change with arbitrary small arc-stack pullbacks, not only geometric points.

nodes.title: Finitary maps and open immersions
nodes.statement: A map f:Y→X is finitary if, for every completed filtered colimit A=colim A_i of strict rings, the square colim Y(A_i)→Y(A) over colim X(A_i)→X(A) is cartesian. An open immersion is a map whose pullback to every Marc(A) is induced by an open subset of M(A). Finitary injections are exactly open immersions.
hypotheses: The condition is relative; it is not absolute filtered continuity of Y in an arbitrary base.
proofSteps: Establish composition, pullback, cancellation against a finitary map and stability under colimits over X directly from the cartesian condition.

For |a|<r use the infimum norm description of filtered colimits to prove openness is finitary. Conversely compact clopen neighbourhood approximation at strict points turns a finitary injection into an open subset.

sources.match: Relative continuity characterizes the maps used by finitary left adjoints.

acceptance: Use the relative square in every base-change statement.

api.name: finitary_stability
api.statement: Finitary maps compose, pull back, and are closed under colimits in the slice.

api.name: finitary_cancellation
api.statement: If g and g∘f are finitary then f is finitary.

api.name: open_iff_finitary_injection
api.statement: A monomorphism is finitary exactly when it is an open immersion.

tests.name: identity
tests.statement: Every identity is finitary even when X itself has no absolute continuity property.

tests.name: open_inequality
tests.statement: The locus |a|<r is finitary, including its empty and full special cases.

tests.name: nonopen_point
tests.statement: A closed point which is not open in a complex interval is not a finitary injection into that interval.

uses.how: Open extension by zero is a finitary left adjoint.
Finitary maps to affine space admit effective left adjoints.

nodes.title: Finitary adjoints and excision
nodes.statement: For finitary f, the derived left adjoint f♯ to f* preserves finitary sheaves and satisfies the projection formula. For an open j:U→X with closed complement i:Z→X, j_!=j♯ and j_!j*M→M→i_*i*M is an exact triangle. The loci |2|>1 and |2|≤1 give the archimedean/nonarchimedean excision decomposition.
hypotheses: X is a small arc-stack and M lies in Dfin(X,Z).
proofSteps: Construct the adjoint in the enhanced slice sheaf category and use composition of finitary maps to retain finitarity.
Check the projection formula on free generators. Identify the open/closed localization on strict bases, then descend the triangle; apply it to the two norm loci.

sources.match: Left adjoints and the open/closed triangle precede the motivic construction.

acceptance: Verify j_! has zero restriction to the complementary closed substack.
Do not treat the |2| threshold as a choice of a residue-characteristic prime.

nodes.title: Effective motivic sheaves
nodes.statement: Deff_mot(X) is the full subcategory of Dfin(X,Z) on ball-invariant objects: M(A)→M(A⟨T⟩₁) is an equivalence for every Banach ring A over X, where A⟨T⟩₁ is the free uniform Banach A-algebra with |T|≤1. Its tensor product is the ball localization of the derived tensor product.
hypotheses: X is a small arc-stack; all coefficients here are integral étale coefficients.
proofSteps: Define the local objects for the displayed maps; use uniformization to remove any ambiguity in the free ball algebra.

Use finite-dimensional proper base change and the strict basis to test ball invariance on nondiscrete algebraically closed Banach fields; this also proves closure under colimits. Import the Berkovich closed-disc tree geometry and the requested residue Galois bounds for the dimension estimate.

sources.match: Effective motives impose closed-unit-ball invariance inside finitary sheaves.

acceptance: Prove d(C⟨T⟩₁)≤3; the complex case has bound 2, the nonarchimedean tree contributes 1 and residue Galois dimension at most 2.

api.name: effective_field_test
api.statement: Ball invariance can be tested at nondiscrete algebraically closed Banach fields.

api.name: effective_pullback
api.statement: Pullback preserves effective motives and their localized tensor product.

api.name: effective_colimits
api.statement: Effective objects are closed under colimits in Dfin.

tests.name: complex_point
tests.statement: At Marc(C) for the usual complex field, effective motives are D(Z).

tests.name: nonarch_units
tests.statement: The reduced multiplicative group is an effective object, although ordinary units retain ball-dependent one-units.

tests.name: integral_not_rational

nodes.title: Explicit ball localization
nodes.statement: The inclusion Deff_mot(X)⊂Dfin(X,Z) has a symmetric monoidal left adjoint L_B. On a strict ring A, (L_B M)(A)=|[n]↦M(A⟨Δⁿ⟩)|, with Δⁿ=Bⁿ and the ordered-coordinate cosimplicial structure. The same formula holds on analytic finite-cohomological-dimension A. This is a presentable monoidal Verdier quotient with kernel the localizing tensor ideal generated by B-contractible objects.
hypotheses: B-contractible means an endomorphism-valued ball homotopy joining the identity to zero.
Use the ordered-coordinate simplex model; naive barycentric coordinate formulas need not be contractive over archimedean rings.
proofSteps: Use finite ball dimension and proper base change to make the realization a finitary sheaf. The standard cosimplicial homotopies identify the two endpoints, prove ball invariance, and prove L_B²≃L_B.

Identify its kernel using the cones of M→Hom(Bⁿ,M); these cones are B-contractible. Apply the presentable monoidal-quotient extension requested from E5, rather than only the small stable Verdier quotient.

sources.match: The ball singular construction computes a localization with a tensor-ideal kernel.

acceptance: Prove both the unit universal property and idempotence.
Specify the spectral variant needed by BM.6 using the same localization.

api.name: ball_localization_values
api.statement: Evaluation on strict and analytic finite-dimensional bases has the displayed realization formula.

api.name: ball_localization_tensor
api.statement: L_B(M⊗N) agrees with L_B M⊗mot L_B N.

tests.name: already_local
tests.statement: The unit M→L_B M is invertible for a ball-invariant M.

tests.name: contractible_zero
tests.statement: A B-contractible object localizes to zero.

tests.name: simplex_zero
tests.statement: Δ⁰ is the base and Δ¹ is the unit ball with the distinct 0 and 1 endpoint maps; they become homotopic after localization.

nodes.title: Rational homotopy t-structure
nodes.statement: Deff_mot(X,Q) is closed under truncations in Dfin(X,Q). Its induced t-structure is the rational homotopy t-structure.
hypotheses: X is a small arc-stack; the archimedean and nonarchimedean geometric-point arguments are treated separately.
proofSteps: At a nonarchimedean algebraically closed point rational ball cohomology has amplitude [0,1]. The resulting two-column spectral sequence forces each cohomology sheaf of a ball-invariant object to be ball-invariant.
Use the geometric-point ball test and treat the complex locus using ordinary sheaves.

sources.match: Rational ball cohomological dimension one gives truncation stability.

acceptance: Do not use integral truncation stability here: that uses the transfer and torsion results of BM.4.

nodes.title: Free motivic sheaves of open affine domains
nodes.statement: For U⊂Aⁿ_X open, define Zmot[U] by ball-localizing the free derived abelian arc-sheaf on U. It is finitary and represents the functor M↦M(U) on effective motives. It commutes with base change and sends fibre products of such domains over X to tensor products. If X is analytic affine of finite cohomological dimension, these objects generate Deff_mot(X).
hypotheses: n is finite; U is open.
Finitarity of L_B^pre U is a theorem to prove, not an assumption on the representable U.
proofSteps: In the nonarchimedean case exhaust U by subsets invariant under sufficiently small additive balls and take their quotients. In general use the source’s uniform approximation argument to prove finitarity of the ball singular construction.

Apply the localization adjunction for representability. For generation, use bounded closed subsets and neighbourhood continuity to detect fields of finite topological transcendence degree, then arbitrary geometric fields.

sources.match: Open affine domains yield finitary free motives and detect effective sheaves.

acceptance: Check the generator argument uses uniformly bounded dimension before passing to neighbourhood limits.

nodes.title: Effective left adjoints
nodes.statement: If f:Y→Aⁿ_X→X is a composite of a finitary map and a finite-dimensional affine-space projection, then f*:Deff_mot(X)→Deff_mot(Y) has a left adjoint f♯ which commutes with base change and satisfies the projection formula.
hypotheses: The factorization is part of the theorem’s hypotheses; arbitrary maps are not included.
proofSteps: Reduce by hyperdescent to strict bases and to the affine-space projection, using the finitary adjoint already established.
On generators define f♯Zmot[V/Y]=Zmot[V/X]. The product formula gives projection; the same formula gives base change and permits descent of the adjoint.

sources.match: The free-domain generators construct the left adjoint for the admitted factorization.

acceptance: Check n=0 agrees with the finitary left adjoint after localization.
On the complex point verify effective motives are D(Z) by the contraction argument.

nodes.title: One-units
nodes.statement: For a nonarchimedean uniform Banach ring A, let A<1={a:|a|<1} and U¹(A)=1+A<1⊂A×. Let U¹ be the associated arc-sheaf of abelian groups. As a light pinned-library prototype on a normed field K, IsOneUnit(u) means ‖u−1‖<1 for u∈K×; an ultrametric hypothesis gives its subgroup and norm-one API.
hypotheses: The ring version is restricted to the nonarchimedean uniform locus.
For the prototype the NormedField and IsUltrametricDist carriers are the existing Mathlib ones; completeness is unnecessary for the elementary field identities.
proofSteps: Use the strong triangle inequality for multiplication and the geometric-series argument in complete rings for inversion. In a field first show a one-unit has norm one, then use u⁻¹−1=−u⁻¹(u−1).
Sheafify the subgroup inclusion. Keep A<1 distinguished from A≤1: a topologically nilpotent element can have norm equal to one before uniformization.

sources.match: The strict norm threshold defines the subgroup removed from units.

acceptance: Compare the elementary field predicate with the uniform complete-field subgroup.

api.name: one_unit_mul_inv
api.statement: The identity is a one-unit; products and inverses of one-units are one-units.

api.name: one_unit_norm
api.statement: In an ultrametric normed field a one-unit has norm exactly one.

api.name: one_unit_transport
api.statement: An isometric unital field map preserves and reflects one-units; a contractive map preserves them.

tests.name: identity
tests.statement: The unit 1 is a one-unit since its difference from 1 has norm zero.

tests.name: norm_obstruction
tests.statement: A unit of norm different from 1 is not a one-unit in an ultrametric field.

tests.name: minus_one
tests.statement: The unit −1 is a one-unit exactly when ‖2‖<1; in particular norm(2)=1 excludes it. This distinguishes <1 from ≤1.

uses.how: Its sheaf quotient removes ball-dependent infinitesimal units.
The nonunital ideal A<1 controls the discarded K-theory.

nodes.title: Reduced multiplicative group
nodes.statement: On a nonarchimedean small arc-stack define Gbar_m as the quotient G_m/U¹ in arc-sheaves of abelian groups, not the unsheafified pointwise quotient on every Banach ring. The reduction map is the canonical epimorphism from the multiplicative group.
hypotheses: The nonarchimedean locus is |2|≤1 and all ring evaluations use uniformization where required.
proofSteps: Form the abelian sheaf quotient and use the strict basis to compute geometric field values.
Derive natural multiplication, quotient maps and base change from the quotient universal property. Establish finitarity using filtered continuity on strict bases.

sources.match: The reduced group is an arc-sheaf quotient by one-units.

acceptance: At a nonarchimedean geometric field C the value is C×/(1+C<1).

api.name: reduced_units_quotient
api.statement: Maps out are maps from G_m killing U¹.

api.name: reduced_units_pullback
api.statement: The quotient is compatible with base change of small arc-stacks.

api.name: reduced_units_field
api.statement: At an algebraically closed nondiscrete nonarchimedean field it is the displayed quotient of units.

tests.name: one_unit_killed
tests.statement: Every 1+a with |a|<1 maps to the identity.

tests.name: valuation_survives
tests.statement: A pseudouniformizer has nontrivial reduced class, as detected by its absolute value.

tests.name: residue_survives
tests.statement: A norm-one unit with residue different from 1 is not killed; the quotient retains more than the value group.

uses.how: Identifies the reduced free multiplicative-group motive.
Its field value defines the extension class for MGC.

nodes.title: Ball invariance and the reduced free-unit motive
nodes.statement: Gbar_m is finitary and ball-invariant. The tautological section induces Zmot[G_m]/Zmot[*]≃Gbar_m on the nonarchimedean locus.
hypotheses: The reduced free motive is formed using the unit section 1.
proofSteps: Modulo a prime use Kummer torsion and the field-invariant-to-ball-invariant direction: residue-characteristic torsion vanishes and other torsion is étale. Rationally compute on the Berkovich tree, using Pic(C⟨T⟩)=0 and harmonic integral slopes to force constant reduced sections.

Group-complete the free commutative monoid and use characteristic polynomials Symⁿ(G_m)≃Aⁿ⁻¹×G_m for the unreduced group. Pass through the one-unit homotopies to deduce the reduced motive formula; do not assert this characteristic-polynomial isomorphism for Symⁿ(Gbar_m).

sources.match: Kummer classes, tree harmonicity and symmetric polynomials give the reduced free-motive identification.

acceptance: Track the basepoint 1 and reduced summand.
Reproduce the P¹ counterexample to the unstabilized projection formula from Example 4.26.

nodes.title: First Tate twist
nodes.statement: For every small arc-stack X define Z(1)=cofib(Zmot[*]→Zmot[G_m])[−1], using the unit section. Write Z(n)=Z(1)⊗n for n≥0 in the effective category. Over the usual complex point Z(1)≃Z; over the real point the conjugation action is the sign action; on the nonarchimedean locus Z(1)≃Gbar_m[−1].
hypotheses: Negative twists belong to the stable category constructed in BM.8.
proofSteps: Take the reduced motive and its specified cohomological shift. Use the previous reduced free-unit calculation on the nonarchimedean locus and ordinary complex topology on the archimedean locus.
Keep the base-change equivalences coherent so that stabilization can invert this same object.

sources.match: The Tate object is a shifted reduced multiplicative-group motive with different pointwise realizations.

acceptance: Pin the cohomological shift by the equality with Gbar_m[−1], rather than an informal degree convention.

api.name: tate_base_change
api.statement: Pullback carries the base Tate object to the Tate object on the source.

api.name: tate_reduced
api.statement: The nonarchimedean identification is Z(1)[1]≃Gbar_m.

api.name: tate_tensor
api.statement: For nonnegative m,n, Z(m)⊗Z(n)≃Z(m+n).

tests.name: complex_tate
tests.statement: Over C the object is Z in degree zero, not zero.

tests.name: real_sign
tests.statement: Complex conjugation on the real realization acts by −1.

tests.name: nonarch_shift
tests.statement: Over a nonarchimedean point the shift is Gbar_m[−1]; a formula without [−1] fails the defining cofiber identity.

uses.how: Tensoring with this object is proved fully faithful.
This precise object is coherently inverted.

nodes.title: Annulus invariance and compact Tate object
nodes.statement: For an open annulus T(r₁,r₂)⊂G_m with 0<r₁<r₂<∞, Zmot[T]→Zmot[G_m] is an equivalence. If the base X is strictly totally disconnected, Z(1) is compact in Deff_mot(X).
hypotheses: Compactness is asserted on strict bases; general relative rigidity does not imply compact generation.
proofSteps: At an archimedean geometric point, use ordinary homology to compare a nonempty complex annulus with G_m. At a nonarchimedean geometric point, rescale so r₁<1<r₂. For the monic polynomial Tⁿ+Σ_{i<n}a_iT^i with fixed a₀∈T(r₁ⁿ,r₂ⁿ), all roots lie in the annulus exactly when |a_i|<min(r₂^{n−i},|a₀|r₁^{−i}) for 1≤i<n. These inequalities give open-polydisc fibres of Symⁿ(T)→T(r₁ⁿ,r₂ⁿ). Use ball invariance on the fibres and let n grow; the union of the target annuli is G_m.
Use finitarity to compare evaluation on open and closed annuli. A closed annulus is quasicompact of finite cohomological dimension, so evaluation preserves colimits, giving compactness.

sources.match: Newton polygons give annular invariance and compact representability.

acceptance: Check the fibre inequalities control all roots, rather than only the product of roots.
The radius uses the minimum of the two coefficient bounds. Check T²+T/2+4 over C₂ with r₁=1/4,r₂=4: its root of norm 1/8 must be excluded; see source finding E5.

nodes.title: Étale torsion is ball-invariant
nodes.statement: If M∈Dfin(X,Z/n) and |n|≥1 everywhere on X, invariance of M under extensions of algebraically closed Banach fields implies ball invariance.
hypotheses: n≥1; invariance is required for every such field extension over X.
proofSteps: Reduce to a nondiscrete algebraically closed field and the constant Z/n sheaf. On the complex locus use the contractible disc.

On the nonarchimedean ball compute the first direct-image sheaf by Kummer branch labels on finite trees: outgoing labels sum at a branch and vanish on rays ending at the boundary. Peel off terminal intervals to show its cohomology vanishes. Higher terms vanish by the residue-Galois bound.

sources.match: Kummer cohomology on the Berkovich tree supplies the forward torsion implication.

acceptance: Use the |n|≥1 condition when taking Kummer roots of one-units.
Do not invoke the reverse implication before the transfer theorem.

nodes.title: Banach presheaves with transfers
nodes.statement: For a strictly totally disconnected X form a category on uniform Banach algebras over X, with maps A→B given by maps of arc-sheaves of commutative monoids N[Marc(A)/X]→N[Marc(B)/X]. A presheaf with transfer is an additive functor from this category to abelian groups; finitary means commuting with completed filtered colimits of all Banach algebras over X.
hypotheses: Composition is composition of monoid-sheaf maps; it is not defined using scheme finite correspondences.
proofSteps: Use the free commutative monoid adjunction and composition to define the category, its additive functors and ordinary restriction.
Construct the evaluation/trace maps encoded by finite multisets; check identity and composition before deriving sheafification.

sources.match: Transfers are encoded by free arc-monoids on affine Banach objects.

acceptance: State the direction of the algebra morphisms and induced restriction maps explicitly.

api.name: transfer_restriction
api.statement: Restricting along actual Banach maps recovers the underlying presheaf.

api.name: transfer_additivity
api.statement: Disjoint multisets give sums of pullback/trace maps, with multiplicities.

api.name: transfer_composition
api.statement: Composition of multivalued maps agrees with composition of induced transfer maps.

tests.name: identity_transfer
tests.statement: A singleton identity multiset acts as the identity.

tests.name: multiplicity
tests.statement: The multiset consisting of d copies of the identity acts by multiplication by d, including d=0.

tests.name: finite_etale_trace
tests.statement: For a degree-d finite étale map, trace after pullback equals d, without requiring a global ordering of the fibres.

uses.how: Transfers compare field extensions and rational Čech descent.
Finite étale diagrams are summed with multiplicity in the rational inverse.

nodes.title: Curve compactification after shrinking
nodes.statement: Given a smooth connected analytic curve U over a nondiscrete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C and two C-points x,x′, there is a connected open neighbourhood U′⊂U of both points, embedded in a smooth projective C-curve X, with X∖U′ a finite disjoint union of closed discs. One can choose a C-point in each boundary disc.
hypotheses: The assertion allows shrinking U while retaining both marked points.
Choose a proper neighbourhood when necessary so the boundary is nonempty.
proofSteps: Choose a connected affinoid neighbourhood of a path joining the two points and apply van der Put’s normal-affinoid embedding with complement finite nonsingular reduction points.

Refine the formal/analytic neighbourhoods of these smooth reduction points to disjoint closed-disc boundary pieces. Remove them to obtain U′, retaining x,x′ by choosing the neighbourhoods away from these points. This last analytic refinement is a required TB supplier request, not a conclusion already stated in Corollary 1.3.

sources.locator: §6, proof of Lemma 6.4, p. 37; van der Put, Corollary 1.3, p. 159 (proof pp. 159–161)
sources.match: The curve argument needs a shrunken disc-boundary domain; the cited affinoid theorem first gives smooth missing reduction points.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.1, pp. 155–158; Corollary 1.3 and proof, pp. 159–161
sources.match: A normal one-dimensional affinoid embeds in a complete smooth curve with only finitely many nonsingular points missing in reduction.

acceptance: Verify both original points remain in U′.
Do not claim an arbitrary given affinoid has the required disc complement without modification.

nodes.title: Generalized Jacobian with marked trivializations
nodes.statement: For a smooth projective geometrically connected C-curve X and r≥1 distinct C-points Z={z₁,…,z_r}, construct J_Z classifying degree-zero line bundles with a trivialization at each z_i, modulo isomorphism. It is a semiabelian variety with exact sequence 1→G_m^{r−1}→J_Z→Jac(X)→0. For every prime ℓ, [ℓ]:J_Z(C)→J_Z(C) is surjective, including ℓ=char(C).
hypotheses: C is algebraically closed; X and Z satisfy the displayed smoothness and distinctness assumptions.
The trivializations are modulo simultaneous scalar automorphisms, hence the torus rank is r−1.
proofSteps: Use the existing relative Picard/Jacobian roadmap for Pic⁰(X). Over it form the torsor of fibre trivializations at Z and divide by the diagonal scalar action; the fibre is (G_m)^r/G_m. Descend this torsor construction to obtain the representing semiabelian group.

Surjectivity of [ℓ] follows from the torus and abelian-variety cases and the extension sequence. In characteristic ℓ this is surjectivity on algebraically closed points, not an étale-isogeny assertion.

sources.locator: §6, proof of Lemma 6.4, p. 37; compare BLR §9.2, Proposition 3, p. 244 and Example 8, pp. 246–247
sources.match: The transfer proof uses divisibility in a marked Picard extension; the ordinary Jacobian alone does not remember boundary trivializations.

sources.locator: §9.2, Proposition 3, p. 244; Example 8, pp. 246–247; Proposition 10, p. 249
sources.match: Smooth proper Picard varieties and normalization of nodal curves exhibit the abelian and toric components used as background for the marked construction.

acceptance: Construct the representing extension and its C-point moduli equivalence.
The BLR nodal Picard example supports the torus-extension pattern; it is not cited as a direct marked-modulus representability theorem.

api.name: marked_jacobian_moduli
api.statement: C-points are the stated isomorphism classes with tensor-product group law.

api.name: marked_jacobian_exact
api.statement: Forgetting trivializations has kernel G_m^{r−1}.

api.name: marked_jacobian_division
api.statement: Every marked degree-zero class admits an ℓth root for each prime ℓ.

tests.name: one_mark
tests.statement: For r=1 the torus kernel is trivial and J_Z≃Jac(X).

tests.name: two_marks_rational
tests.statement: For X=P¹ and r=2, J_Z≃G_m; the ratio of the two trivializations is the coordinate.

tests.name: diagonal_scalars
tests.statement: Multiplying all trivializations by the same scalar leaves the class unchanged. Without marks the Picard stack retains scalar automorphisms and is not this r≥1 moduli problem.

uses.how: Divides O(x−x′) by a prime while preserving every boundary normalization.
Enables the torsion field-invariance argument.

nodes.title: Prime-divisible curve homotopies
nodes.statement: For a smooth connected curve U over C as above, x,x′∈U(C), and a prime ℓ, there are n≥0 and points x_i,x′_i∈U(C) for which [x]+ℓΣ[x_i] and [x′]+ℓΣ[x′_i] are B-homotopic in N[U].
hypotheses: C is nondiscrete, complete, algebraically closed and nonarchimedean.
Use separated smooth curves without boundary, including the curve models needed in the field-extension argument.
proofSteps: Shrink around x,x′ and compactify with closed-disc boundary. Choose one boundary point per disc and divide O(x−x′) by ℓ in the marked generalized Jacobian.

Use rational-section approximation, requested from the curve/affinoid supplier, to choose a divisor for the root line bundle supported away from the boundary and section value 1 at each mark. Express its positive and negative degree-zero parts as sums of C-points.

Interpolate the two corresponding tautological sections by ts₁+(1−t)s₂. Their ratio is a one-unit on each boundary disc, so this section never vanishes there, and the interpolating effective divisors stay in U.

sources.match: Marked divisibility and boundary-unit interpolation give the homotopy after adding prime multiples.

acceptance: Prove support remains away from the entire boundary discs, not just the marked centres.
Include ℓ equal to the residue characteristic without assuming [ℓ] is étale.

nodes.title: Rational motives of finite-boundary line domains
nodes.statement: Let U,V⊂A¹_C be open with complements in P¹_C finite disjoint unions of closed discs. Then Qmot[U](V) is concentrated in degree zero and is the cokernel of N[U](V×B)⊗Q→N[U](V)⊗Q given by the difference of endpoints. If U has d+1 boundary discs, Qmot[U]≃Q⊕(Gbar_m⊗Q)^d.
hypotheses: C is nondiscrete algebraically closed nonarchimedean; the complement includes a disc around infinity.
proofSteps: Use excision and annulus invariance to split the motive into the unit and boundary reduced-unit summands. Compute mappings using the residue-unit and rational boundary-degree coordinates.

For surjectivity use P_t(T)=∏(T−a_i)^{k_i}−t, with |t| between s₁ and s₂. Choose every k_i so r₁^{k_i}<s₁ and n=Σk_i so r₂ⁿ>s₂. Outside the outer disc the product has norm at least r₂ⁿ; inside the ith deleted disc it has norm at most r₁^{k_i}, since the other centre distances are one. Thus every root lies in U. The resulting boundary-degree vectors span all rational slopes. For injectivity interpolate polynomial coefficients; the Newton inequalities keep roots in the domain when product coordinates agree up to one-units.

sources.match: Explicit boundary slopes identify the rational transfer quotient with the actual motive.

acceptance: An open disc has d=0 and an annulus has d=1.
Use the corrected base P¹_C in the source’s line-domain notation.

Verify the corrected exponent k_i in the inner-disc estimate, the sign T₁−T₂ in the nearby-point ratio, and the d rather than e boundary-coordinate count per annular source; see source findings E1–E4.

nodes.title: Ball-invariant transfer sheafification
nodes.statement: A finitary ball-invariant abelian presheaf with transfers on a strict nonarchimedean base has ball-invariant derived arc-sheafification after inverting every prime ℓ with |ℓ|<1 somewhere on the base. Its reduction modulo n is invariant under algebraically closed field extension. Rationally its values on open and affine domains in A¹_A are already unchanged by derived arc-sheafification.
hypotheses: The presheaf has the full transfer structure of BM.4, not just trace maps for a selected cover.
Keep track of the localized coefficient ring when interpreting the modulo-n assertion.
proofSteps: Compute sheafification through the strict basis and quasi-pro-étale sheafification; retain finitarity.
For torsion reduce a field extension to topological transcendence degree one and use a smooth curve model. A C-section gives injectivity and the prime-divisible homotopy gives surjectivity.
Rational transfers give finite étale descent; on the Berkovich line use the finite-boundary domain calculation to split the two-domain Čech sequence.

sources.match: The curve and line-domain lemmas prove exactly the sheafification needed for free motives.

acceptance: Treat the rational Čech argument separately from the torsion argument.

nodes.title: Explicit free motivic sheaves
nodes.statement: For a finitary arc-sheaf of sets U over a nonarchimedean small arc-stack X, and strict A over X, Zmot[U](A) after inverting all primes ℓ with |ℓ|<1 somewhere on M(A) is the group completion of L_B^pre N[U](A). Rationally the formula also computes values on affine arc-subsets of A¹_A. Modulo n with |n|≥1 everywhere on X, Zmot[U]/n is invariant under algebraically closed field extensions.
hypotheses: The explicit group completion is taken in the animated/spectral sense appropriate to the free abelian object, not only on π₀.
proofSteps: The homology presheaves of the group-completed ball singular monoid have finitary transfers. Apply transfer sheafification to prove the resulting arc-sheaf is ball-invariant.
Identify its universal property with the free effective motive, and use the rational and torsion clauses of the sheafification theorem for the two extra formulas.

sources.match: The free effective motive has a cycle/singular construction with explicit coefficient restrictions.

acceptance: Do not assert the formula integrally without the bad-prime inversion.

nodes.title: Torsion motives and characteristic-prime invertibility
nodes.statement: For M∈Dfin(X,Z/n) and |n|≥1 everywhere, ball invariance is equivalent to invariance under algebraically closed field extension. If |p|_A<1 for a prime p, multiplication by p is invertible in Deff_mot(Marc(A)). If |p|≥1 everywhere on M(A), its p-power torsion subcategory is the left-completed derived category of p-power torsion étale sheaves.
hypotheses: Distinguish the strict Banach norm condition |p|_A<1 from the pointwise condition in the second clause.
proofSteps: The forward direction in the equivalence uses generation by free open-domain motives and the explicit-free modulo-n theorem; combine it with the previously proved reverse direction.
For |p|<1 reduce by geometric descent and tilting of perfectoid arc-sites to characteristic p, where the Artin–Schreier exact sequence and contraction of the additive ball force F_p=0.
On strict bases the remaining torsion objects are ordinary sheaves on a profinite set. Descend and retain left completion.

sources.locator: §6, Corollary 6.6 and Theorem 6.7, p. 39; §1, Proposition 1.5, p. 4
sources.match: The two torsion regimes are distinguished by the norm of the prime.

acceptance: Over a geometric field with residue characteristic p, effective motives are Z[1/p]-linear and prime-to-p torsion is D(Z/n).
At the usual complex point the integral category is D(Z), not its rationalization.

nodes.title: Effective motivic tilting
nodes.statement: For a small arc-stack X with |p|<1 everywhere and tilt X♭, tilting induces Deff_mot(X)≃Deff_mot(X♭); both categories are Z[1/p]-linear.
hypotheses: The tilted arc-stack is formed using the perfectoid basis and its arc-site equivalence.
proofSteps: Use perfectoid arc-descent to identify sites. Ordinary ball invariance implies perfectoid-ball invariance by filtered continuity.
Conversely compare the usual ball to its p-power-root tower; trace divided by p gives compatible splittings after p is inverted, so perfectoid-ball invariance implies ordinary ball invariance.

sources.match: Tilting preserves precisely the ball-local objects once p is invertible.

acceptance: Verify the inverse direction, rather than merely transporting the sheaf category.

nodes.title: Integral homotopy t-structure
nodes.statement: For every small arc-stack X, Deff_mot(X) is closed under the truncations of Dfin(X,Z), hence inherits the integral homotopy t-structure.
hypotheses: Use the intrinsic rational and torsion effective subcategories with their already proved truncation stability.
proofSteps: Apply the arithmetic triangle M→M⊗Q→M⊗Q/Z. The remaining issue is that the image of a map from a rational degree-zero effective sheaf to a torsion one is effective.

A field-extension class in that image descends by finitarity to a topologically finite-type algebra over the smaller algebraically closed field, which admits a section. This proves field-invariance of the image; the torsion criterion finishes.

sources.match: The rational-to-torsion image argument closes the integral truncation proof.

acceptance: Do not infer integral truncation stability merely by separately rationalizing and reducing modulo primes without controlling the connecting image.

nodes.title: Tate permutation homotopies
nodes.statement: Every permutation acts trivially on Z(1)⊗n in the homotopy category, for every n≥0 and every small arc-stack. This is the noncoherent assertion used before cancellation; the coherent enhancement is deduced after cancellation.
hypotheses: Keep the Koszul sign: the swap on Gbar_m⊗Gbar_m is −1 because Z(1)=Gbar_m[−1].
proofSteps: Identify the reduced motive of A²∖{0} with Z(2)[3] using the two standard affine charts.

Elementary unipotents act by ball homotopies; they generate SL₂. Reduce coordinate interchange to diag(−1,1). Multiplication by −1 is trivial on the reduced free G_m motive because the total multiplicity is zero. Reduce general permutations to adjacent transpositions.

sources.locator: §7, Lemma 7.3 and discussion preceding its proof, p. 43
sources.match: The elementary homotopy assertion precedes the coherent consequence.

acceptance: Do not use cancellation in this lemma’s proof.
The reduced G_m swap and the Tate swap have different signs.

nodes.title: Rational cancellation inverse
nodes.statement: Over a nondiscrete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C, for each finitary sheaf of sets U and i≥0, construct a natural operation from π_i Hom(Qmot[(G_m,*)],Qmot[U×(G_m,*)]) to eventually defined sequences in π_i Qmot[U]. Its composite with the Tate unit is the constant sequence, it kills the basepoint summand, and its other composite becomes the identity using Tate interchange.
hypotheses: A sequence is identified after restricting to all sufficiently large integers N.
Use étale multivalued spaces with finite geometric fibres and multiplicities; these étale spaces may be nonseparated as points collide.
proofSteps: Represent a class on a closed annulus times a subdivided simplicial sphere using the explicit-free formula. Form Y₁ from the Nth-root-of-unity discs and Y₂ from p₁^N=p₂ in the multivalued graph. For sufficiently large N both fibre over étale spaces with finite geometric fibres and open-ball fibres; the étale spaces need not be separated.
Sum the induced maps to N[U] with multiplicities and take their difference. On the unit image the counts are N and N−1, hence the difference is one; on the basepoint summand they coincide.
Check invariance under all representing homotopies and refinements. Use the noncoherent swap lemma twice to prove the other composite is the identity.

sources.match: The eventual-sequence construction gives both inverse identities and handles multiplicity collisions.

acceptance: Check N−(N−1)=1 including residue-characteristic multiplicities.
No claim that a fixed N works for every homotopy class.
Allow the nonseparated étale spaces needed at collisions; finiteness of geometric fibres does not make these finite étale morphisms.

nodes.title: Cancellation over any base
nodes.statement: For every small arc-stack X, tensoring by Z(1):Deff_mot(X)→Deff_mot(X) is fully faithful; equivalently M→Hom(Z(1),M⊗Z(1)) is an equivalence for every effective M.
hypotheses: There is no field or smoothness assumption on X.
proofSteps: Use the annulus model and proper base change to compare the relevant internal Homs with ambient derived sheaves. Restrict to strict bases; compactness of Tate reduces to their geometric stalks.

At the complex point Tate is the unit; with torsion coefficients apply the torsion étale comparison. In the rational nonarchimedean case apply the explicit eventual inverse on free generators. Combine rational and torsion tests integrally and descend.

sources.locator: §7, Theorem 7.1 and Remark 7.2, pp. 40–43; §1, Theorem 1.9, p. 6
sources.match: The pointwise proof and compact Tate object establish cancellation over arbitrary small arc-stacks.

acceptance: Prove the adjunction unit equivalence, not only injectivity on π₀.
After cancellation, deduce homotopy-coherent triviality of the symmetric-group actions using the discrete endomorphism space of the unit.

nodes.title: Symmetric powers and projective motives
nodes.statement: For n≥0, Symⁿ(Q(1))≃Q(n). The cofiber of Zmot[Pⁿ⁻¹]→Zmot[Pⁿ] is Z(n)[2n] for n≥1. There is a canonical decomposition Qmot[BG_m]≃⊕_{n≥0}Q(n)[2n]; Pⁿ maps to the summands with 0≤i≤n through the class of O(1).
hypotheses: The splitting asserted here is rational; the cell cofiber is integral.
BG_m free motives use left Kan extension from smooth charts.
proofSteps: Use coherent Tate symmetry after cancellation to identify rational symmetric powers. Construct the projective cell cofibers using the affine chart and A¹-fibration over Pⁿ⁻¹.

Animate the augmentation-ideal filtration on the group algebra of a 1-connective abelian group. Its graded terms have increasing connectivity. The projective cell filtration splits it and proves convergence to the displayed direct sum.

sources.match: Symmetry and increasing connectivity identify the classifying-space motive and its finite projective truncations.

acceptance: P⁰ maps to the n=0 unit summand; P¹ has the two expected summands.
The result is a direct sum, not an unverified product decomposition.

nodes.title: Spectral motivic K-theory
nodes.statement: Let Kcn(A) be the connective K-theory spectrum of the underlying abstract ring, obtained by E-infinity group completion of finite projective modules. Define Kmot as its universal ball-invariant arc-sheaf of spectra. Kmot is finitary and has its induced E-infinity ring structure.
hypotheses: This integral object is spectrum-valued, not an object of D(Z) by definition.
The spectral ball-localization uses the same site and test balls.
proofSteps: Import the connective multiplicative ring K-theory model from K.2:plus with the precise group-completion enhancement requested there.

Use the Breen–Deligne resolution contract requested from E5:animation to resolve the sheafified group completion by classifying spaces of products of GL_n, and these by GL_n charts. Their free ball-invariant spectral sheaves are finitary by the free-domain theorem.
Apply symmetric monoidal spectral localization to obtain the universal E-infinity structure.

sources.match: Spectral group completion and the GL-chart resolution establish finitarity before rationalization.

acceptance: The map Kcn→Kmot is universal among ball-invariant arc-sheaves of spectra.
Do not replace the integral spectrum by ordinary chain complexes.

api.name: motivic_k_universal
api.statement: Maps from Kmot to a local spectral sheaf correspond to maps from Kcn.

api.name: motivic_k_multiplication
api.statement: The map from Kcn is multiplicative and Kmot is an E-infinity ring sheaf.

api.name: motivic_k_finitary
api.statement: Evaluation on the strict basis commutes with filtered colimits.

tests.name: rank_unit
tests.statement: A rank-one free module maps to the multiplicative unit and rank-zero to zero.

tests.name: ball_local

Supplies the universal comparison map for explicit evaluations.

nodes.title: Rational flag invariants
nodes.statement: The Σ_n-invariants in Qmot[GL_n/G_m^n], with the permutation action of the normalizer, are Q[0].
hypotheses: n≥1 and coefficients are rational so finite-group invariants are direct summands.
proofSteps: Induct on n: Σ_{n−1}-invariants identify with Qmot[Pⁿ⁻¹] via the smooth projection and the preceding flag fibre.

Use cancellation to make endomorphisms of its finite Tate decomposition upper triangular with rational diagonal. The required classical flag realization, requested in the MC.2 direction, identifies which diagonal entries of the averaging idempotent are one: precisely the degree-zero entry.

sources.match: The flag calculation reduces rational K-theory to the maximal torus and fixes the averaging idempotent.

acceptance: Verify n=1 directly and n=2 using the two Tate cells of P¹.
Record the realization input rather than asserting arbitrary realizations are conservative.

nodes.title: Canonical rational motivic K-splitting
nodes.statement: The multiplicative line-bundle map Qmot[BG_m]→Kmot⊗Q is an equivalence. The separated descending motivic filtration has graded pieces Q(n)[2n] for n≥0 and is canonically split by Adams operations: ψ² acts as 2ⁿ on weight n, giving Kmot⊗Q≃⊕_{n≥0}Q(n)[2n].
hypotheses: General ring E-infinity Adams functoriality is the requested S.6 extension; its existing regular-scheme API alone is insufficient.
proofSteps: Use the normalizer of the maximal torus and the rational flag-invariant calculation to compare the GL_n classifying spaces to the symmetric algebra of BG_m. Pass to group completion.

Transfer the convergent augmentation filtration from BG_m. Distinct eigenvalues 2ⁿ give canonical weight projectors compatible with finite stages; increasing connectivity identifies the colimit splitting with the direct sum.

sources.locator: §8, Proposition 8.5 and Corollary 8.6, pp. 45–46; §1, Theorem 1.7(i)–(ii), p. 5
sources.match: The rational comparison is split by distinct Adams eigenvalues, not by a noncanonical chosen basis.

acceptance: Check ψ² has eigenvalues 1,2,4 in the first three weights.
State multiplication sends weights (m,n) to m+n.

nodes.title: One-unit K-cofiber
nodes.statement: For a nonarchimedean uniform Banach ring A admitting a topologically nilpotent unit T with a compatible unbounded sequence of roots, set I=A<1. Import its Tor-unital almost-module K-theory K(I) from RT.5 and define E_K(A)=cofib(K(I)→K(A)); define E_Kcn similarly using connective covers. E_K commutes with completed filtered colimits within this root-admitting class. On totally disconnected A, E_Kcn≃E_K.
hypotheses: The root data are retained through the diagrams used for continuity.
K(I) is the unitization-independent nonunital K-theory, not K₀ of the abstract group 1+I.
proofSteps: Use the RT.5 flat idempotent ideal/almost-category theorem and the K.5 excision contract to identify the nonunital K-spectrum, independent of an ambient unitization.

Set B=Z⊕I and localize at T. TT invariance of supported perfect complexes under derived closed-fibre-preserving completion gives completed continuity after taking the cofiber. For totally disconnected rings reduce to fields and use the missing valuation-ring connective/nonconnective contract recorded as a gap.

sources.locator: §8, discussion before Proposition 8.7 and Proposition 8.8, pp. 46–47
sources.match: The imported almost-category theorem defines the nonunital term and completion invariance gives continuity.

acceptance: Check independence of unitization.
Verify the derived closed fibre hypothesis before invoking TT.

api.name: unit_k_natural
api.statement: A root-compatible contractive map induces a natural map of cofiber sequences.

tests.name: zero_ideal
tests.statement: For I=0, the nonunital K-term is zero and the cofiber is K(A).

tests.name: field_model
tests.statement: For a valued field C, K(I)=fib(K(O_C)→K(k)), with the maps to K(C) retained.

tests.name: root_guard
tests.statement: For A=Q_p, I=pZ_p has I/I²≃F_p, so Tor₁ over Z⊕I of the two augmentation modules Z is nonzero. This A lacks arbitrarily deep roots of a pseudouniformizer and does not satisfy this Tor-unital root-admitting construction.

uses.how: Identifies motivic K-theory at strict bases and geometric fields.
The support exact sequence supplies the extra Laurent-series summand.

nodes.title: One-unit connective K-theory contracts
nodes.statement: The universal ball-invariant arc-sheaf under A↦Kcn(A<1) is zero on the root-admitting nonarchimedean class.
hypotheses: Use the same nonunital and connective-cover conventions as E_K.
proofSteps: Choose the functorial unitization Z⊕A<1. The map GL_n(Z⊕A<1)→GL_n(Z) has ball-contractible fibres by scaling the infinitesimal matrix part.
Apply group-completion resolution and ball localization to kill its relative connective K-theory.

sources.match: Matrix fibres exhibit the contraction of the discarded connective K-term.

acceptance: Check contraction preserves invertibility throughout the unit ball.

nodes.title: Perfectoid analytic K-cofiber descent
nodes.statement: For perfectoid A with |p|_A<1, E_K(A) is an analytic sheaf. If all sheaves on M(A) are Postnikov complete, E_K(A)⊗Q is the value of a finitary ball-invariant arc-hypersheaf and equals Kmot(A)⊗Q.
hypotheses: Retain the Postnikov hypothesis for the rational identification, not for analytic descent itself.
proofSteps: Identify fib(K(A<1)→K(A)) with continuous K-theory of torsion almost A≤1-modules using two Verdier sequences.

Closed subsets yield idempotent complete almost algebras; localization on two closed pieces gives a categorical excision square. Continuous K-theory sends this to a pullback, proving analytic descent.

Rational trace descent gives profinite étale descent. Use Postnikov completeness to compare the analytic/profinite reconstruction with arc-hypersheafification. Perfectoid-ball invariance reduces by support excision to the valuation-ring A¹-invariance contract recorded as a gap.

sources.match: Torsion almost modules give analytic descent; the rational arc comparison needs Postnikov convergence.

acceptance: Finite covering dimension of M(A) is a sufficient Postnikov condition through the requested E2 theorem.
Do not claim analytic descent alone proves unbounded arc-hyperdescent.

nodes.title: Explicit motivic K-theory on strict bases
nodes.statement: Fix a set S of primes. On nonarchimedean strict A with |ℓ|≥1 everywhere for every prime ℓ∉S, E_K(A)[1/S] is finitary, ball-invariant and an arc-sheaf of spectra, and equals Kmot(A)[1/S]. In particular for nondiscrete algebraically closed nonarchimedean C of residue-characteristic exponent p, Kmot(C)≃E_K(C)[1/p], with p=1 in residue characteristic zero.
hypotheses: The spectral field formula uses the geometric root property; no arbitrary Banach-ring integral formula is asserted.
proofSteps: Use one-unit connective K-vanishing and continuity to compare E_Kcn with the universal localized object.
Torsion field invariance uses Gabber–Suslin rigidity: the available L.2 request handles its henselian part, and the full geometric contract is the recorded missing Part-II supplier.
Rationally use perfectoid descent for |p|<1, and the KH analytic-descent route for equal characteristic zero. Combine rational and torsion data and apply the strict-basis hypersheaf criterion.

sources.locator: §8, Theorem 8.9 and proof, pp. 47–49; §1, Theorem 1.7(iii), p. 5
sources.match: The cofiber identifies the universal sheaf after exactly the necessary prime inversion.

acceptance: When residue characteristic is zero, [1/p] is the identity.
The prime set is controlled pointwise over the entire strict base.

nodes.title: Integral field-cofiber E-infinity structure
nodes.statement: For a nondiscrete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field C, E_K(C) without inverting the residue characteristic has a natural E-infinity K(C)-algebra structure.
hypotheses: This conclusion equips a cofiber with an additional structure; it does not come from a general rule assigning ring structures to cofibers.
proofSteps: Away from p use the equivalence with Kmot. For residue characteristic p>0 request K(O_C)^∧p≃K(C)^∧p and K(k)^∧p≃Z_p for perfect k; these imply E_K(C)^∧p≃Z_p.

The overlap map to Q_p is rank followed by the scalar inclusion. Glue the two E-infinity K(C)-algebras by arithmetic fracture. If the residue characteristic exponent is 1 only the first piece is needed.

sources.match: Prime inversion and p-completion glue to an integral cofiber algebra through the rank map.

acceptance: Check compatibility on the overlap as maps of algebras, not only homotopy groups.

nodes.title: Root-free analytic KH-cofiber
nodes.statement: For every analytic nonarchimedean Banach ring A the root-free homotopy K-theory cofiber E_KH(A)=cofib(KH(A<1)→KH(A)) is an analytic sheaf. If all sheaves on M(A) are Postnikov complete, E_KH(A)⊗Q is finitary, ball-invariant, arc-hypercomplete and equals Kmot(A)⊗Q. For totally disconnected A this is E_K(A)⊗Q.
hypotheses: The definition of the relative KH term uses its truncating/ideal-independent model and ball localization; it does not assume the raw ideal was Tor-unital.
The needed general KH cdh-descent supplier has no live routed roadmap; this contract is a recorded gap.
proofSteps: Import KH as the A¹-invariant version of nonconnective K-theory and its truncating property through the K.5 request. Noetherian approximation reduces analytic descent to formal models and admissible blowups.

Use the missing general cdh-descent theorem for KH. The pro-cdh theorem followed by ball localization is an alternative proof route recorded in the same ownership gap, rather than an extra simultaneous requirement.

Use rational finite étale traces and Postnikov convergence as in the perfectoid argument. The valuation-ring A¹-invariance contract gives the ball calculation and the replacement of KH by K on totally disconnected bases.

sources.match: The truncating KH model removes the root hypothesis and formal-model descent supplies the analytic sheaf property.

acceptance: Keep both the root-free scope and the Postnikov restriction on the rational identification.
Do not replace integral KH cdh descent by a height-one-localized K-theory statement.

nodes.title: Smooth-completion motivic K-comparison
nodes.statement: If C is a nondiscrete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field and A is a Banach C-algebra such that A≤1 is the completion of a smooth O_C-algebra, then Kmot(A)⊗Q≃cofib(K(A<1)→K(A))⊗Q, naturally in A.
hypotheses: The hypothesis is on the actual ring of elements of norm at most one, not merely the existence of some unrelated smooth model.
The root-admitting interpretation of K(A<1) uses the roots available from the algebraically closed coefficient field.
proofSteps: Apply analytic KH-cofiber descent to the smooth formal model. Use the valuation-ring homotopy-invariance and smooth-model K/KH comparison contract recorded in the supplier gap to replace the relative KH-cofiber by the K-cofiber.

Use TT to compare the supported terms through completion. Establish the finite-dimensional spectral/Postnikov hypothesis on the smooth affinoid before invoking the rational arc comparison. The result is precisely the cofiber formula displayed in the statement.

sources.locator: §1, Theorem 1.7(iv), p. 5; §8, Proposition 8.8 and Theorem 8.13, pp. 47, 49–50
sources.match: The smooth formal-model formula is obtained from the supported K-theory square and completion.

acceptance: State and verify Kmot(A)_Q≃E_K(A)_Q with the natural map from connective K(A); do not interchange the source and target of the nonunital inclusion.
Check the case A=C and the closed unit ball of a smooth formal O_C-model.

nodes.title: Stable motivic sheaves
nodes.statement: Dmot(X)=Deff_mot(X)[Z(1)⊗−1] is the symmetric monoidal presentable stable infinity-category universally inverting Tate. It is the colimit of successive Tate tensor functors in PrL and equivalently the limit of internal-Hom functors: objects are sequences (M_n) with M_n≃Hom(Z(1),M_{n+1}). The map Deff_mot(X)→Dmot(X) is fully faithful.
hypotheses: X is any small arc-stack.
Coherent Tate symmetry is supplied after cancellation, before applying tensor inversion.
proofSteps: Deduce coherent permutation triviality from cancellation and the discrete endomorphism space of the unit, then apply the existing formal-inversion theorem.
Use the colimit/adjoint-limit comparison in presentable categories to obtain the sequence model. Cancellation identifies an effective M with the sequence M(n), proving full faithfulness.

sources.match: Coherent inversion and cancellation identify the stable category and its effective subcategory.

acceptance: Verify the sequence bonding maps have Hom(Z(1),−), not tensor by Z(1).

api.statement: A colimit-preserving symmetric monoidal functor out of Deff with invertible Tate factors uniquely through Dmot.

api.name: stable_twists
api.statement: For all integers m,n the twists satisfy Z(m)⊗Z(n)≃Z(m+n).

api.name: stable_effective_embedding

tests.statement: At the complex point stabilization does not change D(Z), since Tate is the unit.
