uses.how: Makes the projective-line duality twist invertible.
Hosts rigid categories, algebraic étale comparison and nearby cycles.

nodes.title: Projective-line duality
nodes.statement: For f:P¹_X→X, f♯≃f_*⊗Z(1)[2] on Dmot(P¹_X). Consequently f_* has the stable projection formula.
hypotheses: X is any small arc-stack; f♯ is the effective smooth adjoint extended to the stabilization.
proofSteps: Construct the unit from the G_m-torsor O(Δ) on P¹×_X P¹, trivialized off the diagonal. Construct the counit using reduced P¹-cohomology and the invertible Tate object.
Check both triangle identities after restriction to affine-chart generators and geometric fibres; the remaining endomorphism is the identity on the unit by the explicit reduced G_m computation.

sources.match: Diagonal and reduced-cohomology maps yield the duality adjunction.

acceptance: Track both [2] and Z(1).
Explain why this assertion does not contradict the effective-category counterexample.

nodes.title: Stable affine pushforward
nodes.statement: For f:Marc(B)→Marc(A) of finite cohomological dimension, if Marc(B) embeds into a finite-dimensional ball over Marc(A), then f_* on stable motives preserves all colimits, commutes with every base change and satisfies the projection formula. The same holds arc-locally on the target for such maps.
hypotheses: The embedding and finite-dimension hypotheses are explicit; the broader proper result follows after point rigidity.
proofSteps: Apply effective proper base change levelwise in the sequence model of stabilization.
Reduce the projection formula to geometric fields and then to a one-dimensional ball. Embed it in P¹ and apply projective-line duality and open/closed excision. Descend the resulting identity.

sources.match: The stable projective-line calculation upgrades the affine proper projection formula.

acceptance: Check each level of the stable sequence is preserved by pushforward.

nodes.title: Six operations on small arc-stacks
nodes.statement: The assignment X↦Dmot(X) extends to a six-functor formalism on small arc-stacks for the class of !-able maps constructed by the abstract extension theorem from finite-cohomological-dimension affine maps. Open immersions are !-able with j_! left adjoint to j*. Étale maps, meaning finitary maps with finite geometric fibres, are cohomologically étale. Smooth boundaryless maps of analytic K-spaces are cohomologically smooth.
hypotheses: Do not assert every map is !-able.
For the analytic smooth statement K is a nondiscrete Banach field and the morphism is without boundary.
proofSteps: Apply the AS.0 construction principle and its extension theorem to the affine pushforward data, verifying the base-change, projection and descent axioms from BM.1–BM.8.
Exhaust |a|<1 by affine |a|≤c pieces to compute j_!. Étale maps reduce to finite fibres and the smooth case reduces to affine space/P¹ duality on local charts.

sources.match: The abstract construction is imported; this target verifies and applies it to Berkovich motives.

acceptance: Export adjunctions, projection, base change, composition and localization as coherent functorial identities.
Keep boundaryless smoothness in the statement of analytic duality.

nodes.title: Stable motivic tilting
nodes.statement: If |p|<1 everywhere on a small arc-stack X, there is a symmetric monoidal equivalence Dmot(X)≃Dmot(X♭) compatible with effective motives and Tate twists.
hypotheses: Use the same tilted-site construction as effective tilting.
proofSteps: Transport the reduced multiplicative-group description through tilting and identify the Tate object.
Apply the universal property of tensor inversion to the effective equivalence and its inverse.

sources.match: Effective tilting preserves the object inverted in stable motives.

acceptance: Check the equivalence carries Z(n) to Z(n) for negative as well as positive n.

nodes.title: Compact generators at geometric points
nodes.statement: For a nondiscrete algebraically closed Banach field C, Dmot(C) is compactly generated with compact unit and compact objects exactly the dualizable objects. In equal characteristic, given a splitting k→C of its residue field, the Zmot[X_C](−j), for X smooth projective over k and j≥0, are compact generators. The discrete algebraically closed case is supplied by BM.10.
hypotheses: The good-reduction generator description requires both equal characteristic and the chosen splitting.
proofSteps: Use stable tilting to reduce to equal characteristic. Proper smooth duality shows the displayed generators are dualizable; the unit is compact, so they are compact.
Detect a vanishing motive by induction on topological transcendence degree of geometric field extensions. Type-(4) points reduce by balls and type-(3) by annuli and Tate twists.

For the remaining residue-transcendence case use smooth finite-type models and the L5 alterations theorem to produce projective compactifications with normal-crossing boundary after alteration. Trace descent and localization reduce to lower dimension. Do not replace alterations by resolution of singularities.

sources.match: Good-reduction projective generators are obtained by geometric-field induction and alterations.

acceptance: Verify the torsion subcategory is detected by the unit before doing the rational induction.
Use compact=dualizable only after proving the unit compact.

nodes.title: Proper pushforward after geometric rigidity
nodes.statement: For every proper 0-truncated map of locally finite cohomological dimension between small arc-stacks, stable f_* preserves colimits, commutes with arbitrary base change and satisfies the projection formula. Reapplying the AS.0 extension procedure with this proper class gives the enlarged class of !-able maps.
hypotheses: The basic objects for testing !-ability remain affine arc-stacks.
proofSteps: Use the stable sequence model and finitary proper base change for colimits and base change locally.

Check projection at geometric points. At each such point the target category is compactly generated by dualizables, so linearity extends from dualizable generators to all objects. Apply the abstract extension with this verified proper class.

sources.locator: §10, Corollary 10.2 and its following discussion, pp. 53–54
sources.match: Geometric compact generation removes the earlier finite-ball-embedding restriction.

acceptance: Do not move this projection formula before the proof of geometric-point rigidity.

nodes.title: Compact morphisms of relative motives
nodes.statement: If X is analytic affine of finite cohomological dimension, or satisfies the qcqs fibre hypotheses of the relative-rigidity target, and U⊂V⊂Aⁿ_X are open with U→V factoring through a quasicompact subset K, then Zmot[U]→Zmot[V] is a compact morphism. Such maps and their negative Tate twists provide compact-morphism exhaustions of generators, and tensor products of generating compact morphisms are compact.
hypotheses: Compact morphism is the E5 categorical notion, not a synonym for having compact source and target.
proofSteps: The induced map on mapping functors factors through evaluation at K, which preserves filtered colimits by finite-dimensional continuity.

Exhaust each open V by relatively compact U and use open affine-domain generation. In the general one-point quotient case use the profinite quotient argument of ECD 21.9 through the C8 request and invariant open domains. Tensor products correspond to products of these strict inclusions.

sources.match: Strict domain inclusions provide the compact morphisms needed for compact assembly.

acceptance: Check generators are exhausted by compact transitions even when the generators themselves are not compact.

nodes.title: Rigidity over analytic bases
nodes.statement: If A is analytic of finite cohomological dimension, Dmot(Marc(A)) is rigid. More generally this holds for a qcqs arc-sheaf X of finite cohomological dimension such that each x∈|X| is the image of a quasi-pro-étale map Marc(C(x))→X from a nondiscrete algebraically closed Banach field. Here rigid has the E5 presentable-monoidal meaning, including compact unit and the trace-class criterion; compact generation is not asserted.
hypotheses: The pointwise quasi-pro-étale presentation is an additional hypothesis in the general qcqs case.
proofSteps: Use compact-morphism generator exhaustions and the stable compact-assembly criterion to prove categorical dualizability. Finite cohomological dimension makes the unit compact.

At a point X=Marc(C)/G, descend compact objects together with their duals and duality maps along finite-level profinite quotients using quasi-pro-étale monadicity and the strongly continuous compact-object theorem.

Spread fibrewise dualizables to closed neighbourhoods. Extend their restrictions from countable unions of closed neighbourhoods by zero to obtain trace-class exhaustions, and apply the rigid-category criterion.

sources.match: Compact assembly and trace-class spreading prove relative rigidity without a compact-generation claim.

acceptance: Verify all right adjoints in the filtered descent preserve colimits before using compact-object descent.

nodes.title: Quasi-pro-étale monadicity
nodes.statement: For a proper quasi-pro-étale f:Y→X, f_* induces Dmot(Y)≃Mod_{f_*Z}(Dmot(X)). If Y=lim_i Y_i is a cofiltered limit of such maps, then Dmot(Y)≃colim_i Dmot(Y_i) in presentable stable categories.
hypotheses: No surjectivity assumption is needed; the relevant conservative functor is f_* on source objects.
proofSteps: Fibres are profinite sets, so f has cohomological dimension zero, colimit-preserving pushforward and projection. Global sections on profinite fibres detect source objects, proving f_* conservative.
Apply the exact Barr–Beck–Lurie criterion and identify the monad by projection. Finitarity gives f_*Z=colim_i f_i*Z; the E5 module-base-change theorem gives the categorical colimit.

sources.match: Conservative pushforward and the projection formula identify the module category.

acceptance: Identify which adjoint is conservative.
For an empty fibre the module category over the zero algebra is the zero category.

nodes.title: Weak categorical Künneth
nodes.statement: For X→S←Y with X,Y,S qcqs and satisfying the hypotheses of relative rigidity, exterior tensor product gives a fully faithful functor Dmot(X)⊗_{Dmot(S)}Dmot(Y)→Dmot(X×_S Y).
hypotheses: Only full faithfulness is concluded; essential surjectivity is not part of this theorem.
proofSteps: Relative tensor products of rigid categories are rigid; reduce full faithfulness to the adjunction unit evaluated on tensor generators and then pushed to S.
The resulting identity is f_*M⊗g_*N≃(f×_S g)_*(M⊠N), which follows from proper-base-change/projection identities of the admitted six-functor setting, locally on these qcqs bases.

sources.match: The ordinary Künneth projection identity proves full faithfulness of the relative tensor functor.

acceptance: A statement replacing fully faithful by equivalence is rejected.

nodes.title: Pointwise Artin–Tate motives
nodes.statement: DMT(X) is the full subcategory of Dmot(X) whose pullback to every nondiscrete algebraically closed geometric point Marc(C)→X lies in the localizing stable subcategory generated by all Z(n), n∈Z. The localizing closure includes colimits, shifts and retracts.
hypotheses: This is the pointwise Artin–Tate convention of Definition 10.7.
At a general base it is not defined as the global closure of its Tate objects.
proofSteps: Define the full subcategory using all geometric pullbacks and the explicitly generated fibre categories.
Use tensor closure of the Tate-generated point categories and base-change functoriality to obtain tensor and pullback stability.

sources.match: The mixed Tate condition is tested geometrically, allowing Artin phenomena globally.

acceptance: No general stability under f_! is claimed.

The explicit Dqc models describe these subcategories.

nodes.title: Arc-descent and rigidity of Artin–Tate motives
nodes.statement: X↦DMT(X) is an arc-sheaf of symmetric monoidal presentable stable categories. On strictly totally disconnected X it is generated globally by all Z(n). For X satisfying the relative-rigidity hypotheses, DMT(X) is rigid.
hypotheses: Global Tate generation is asserted for strictly totally disconnected bases, not for arbitrary X.
proofSteps: For an algebraically closed extension C′/C compare compact presentations. A compact transition which factors through a mixed Tate object after extension descends to a finite-transcendence, finite-type algebra and a section back to C; thus the factorization already exists over C.

On strict bases the right adjoint to the Tate-generated inclusion preserves colimits, so its counit is an equivalence by stalks. Repeat compact/trace-class exhaustions inside this subcategory to obtain rigidity.

sources.match: Compact-factorization descent makes the geometric Tate condition local and rigid.

acceptance: Use descent of compact factorizations rather than descent of a chosen arbitrary infinite presentation.

nodes.title: Integral algebraic étale motives
nodes.statement: For a field k, DM_et(k,Z) is the presentable Z-linear stable infinity-category generated by motives of smooth finite-type k-schemes, imposing étale descent and A¹-invariance and then inverting the reduced G_m object shifted by [−1]. Use the tensor induced by products of schemes. Its algebraic Tate object is the shifted reduced G_m motive, agreeing with the convention in BM.3.
hypotheses: The construction is enhanced and presentable; it is not merely the triangulated category of bounded geometric Nisnevich motives.
No unrestricted Galois hyperdescent theorem is part of the definition.
proofSteps: Start with enhanced derived presheaves on Sm/k, impose étale local descent and the A¹ projection equivalences by presentable monoidal localization.

Apply coherent Tate inversion. Use the parent geometric-motive and M.5a transfer constructions only for their actual Nisnevich/geometric range; the étale enhancement and comparison to that partial input are the present target and the explicit M.5a request.

sources.match: The integral presentable étale category must be distinguished from the parent’s geometric triangulated Nisnevich category.

sources.locator: §2.2, pp. 25–27; §5.1, pp. 42–44; Corollaries 5.5.5 and 5.5.7, pp. 55–56 (arXiv v4 pagination)
sources.match: Corollary 5.5.5 compares the with-transfer and h models over fields. Corollary 5.5.7 gives the transfer-free comparison only in characteristic zero or with 2 invertible; the full enhanced integral bridge is an explicit supplier request.

acceptance: Show the stated universal property in presentable symmetric monoidal Z-linear categories.
Document the topology and enhancements in the comparison to the parent construction.
For positive characteristic, retain the coefficient restrictions in the cited transfer-free comparison; Corollary 5.5.5 alone does not compare a transfer-free presentation.

nodes.title: Mapping formulas for algebraic étale motives
nodes.statement: For algebraically closed k, smooth projective X/k and integer j, Map_DM_et(k,Z)(M(X)(−j),Z)_Q≃K(X)_Q^(j)[−2j], and after prime-to-char(k) completion the mapping spectrum is RΓ_proet(X,Zhat_{p′}(j)). These formulas and compact dualizable smooth-projective generators detect the algebraic comparison.
hypotheses: With cohomological shifts and homotopy groups π_i, the rational formula is π_i Map(M(X)(−j),Z)_Q=K_{i+2j}(X)_Q^(j); the shift cannot be suppressed.
Completion and mapping spectra are derived; use p=1 in characteristic zero.
proofSteps: Use the requested M.5a transfer/étale enhancement bridge to the algebraic derived model. Apply Cisinski–Déglise rigidity for torsion and their rational Beilinson comparison on regular schemes; S.6 identifies the gamma-graded terms with Adams weights.

Use étale descent, the prime-to-characteristic torsion rigidity theorem and rational alteration traces together with localization and Tate inversion to obtain smooth-projective compact dualizable generation. The rational use of alteration degrees is legitimate after rationalization; no integral prime-to-coefficient alteration degree is assumed. EDS enhancement gives mapping-spectrum comparisons.

sources.locator: Cisinski–Déglise, Theorem 4.5.2, p. 41; Theorem 5.2.2, p. 44 (proof p. 47); Corollaries 5.5.5 and 5.5.7, pp. 55–56; Scholze, Remark 11.2, p. 57
sources.match: The formula Hom(Q_X,Q_X(j)[q])=Gr^j_γ K_{2j−q}(X)_Q fixes the shift, and torsion rigidity supplies the completed side; the enhanced transfer-free bridge remains requested.

Record the request for the prime-to-characteristic completed/pro-étale realization, rather than dropping the completion.

nodes.title: Discrete algebraically closed field generators
nodes.statement: For algebraically closed k with the trivial Banach norm, Dmot(k) is generated by compact dualizable Zmot[X](−j), where X is smooth projective over k and j∈Z. The unit is compact, so compact objects are precisely the dualizable ones.
hypotheses: The Banach norm is trivial; do not apply the nondiscrete geometric theorem directly to k.
proofSteps: Let K=k((T)) with |T|=1/2. Annulus continuity identifies f_*Z for f:Marc(K)→Marc(k) with Z⊕Z(−1)[−1], a dualizable object.

Apply the geometric-point good-reduction argument over the completed algebraic closure of K, and descend the finite-presentation data together with Artin motives through finite extensions of K. Each finite extension is again a Laurent-series field over k, so the same split-pushforward calculation applies. This gives f♯ on generators, and hence in general, with f♯Z dual to f_*Z and compact. Its unit retract is compact; conservativity of f* and the descended good-reduction generators give the stated generation over k.

sources.match: A Laurent-series extension and its split pushforward prove compact generation at a discrete point.

acceptance: The generator twists here range over every integer.
Together with BM.9 this covers both discrete and nondiscrete algebraically closed Banach fields.
Do not apply the algebraically closed field theorem directly to nonclosed K=k((T)); include the finite-extension Artin generators in the descent argument.

nodes.title: Motivic mapping formulas over a discrete field
nodes.statement: For k algebraically closed with trivial norm, smooth projective X/k and j∈Z, Map_Dmot(k)(Zmot[X](−j),Z)_Q≃K(X)_Q^(j)[−2j], so π_i is K_{i+2j}(X)_Q^(j). After prime-to-characteristic profinite completion the mapping spectrum is RΓ_proet(X,Zhat_{p′}(j)).
hypotheses: Use derived completion and cohomological shifts, with the same π_i grading as in the algebraic mapping input.
proofSteps: Pass to a completed algebraic closure C of k((T)) and apply the smooth-completion K formula. The support localization sequence compares K(X_OC), K(X_C) and K(X).

TT supported excision reduces the special-fibre support term to K(X); its Adams weight shifts by one. Induct on weight to match this extra summand with the Laurent-series f♯Z summand. Torsion maps follow from the effective torsion theorem and inverse limits of finite coefficients.

sources.match: The support term has the weight shift needed to recover algebraic K-theory from good reduction.

acceptance: Check the weight shift in the support term and the Laurent-series [−1] shift together.
Negative rational weights vanish in the specified smooth regular range.
Check the j=1 projective-line summand occurs at π_{−2}, not π_0; see E6 for the omitted source shift.

nodes.title: Berkovich and algebraic étale motives
nodes.statement: For algebraically closed discrete k the canonical symmetric monoidal functor DM_et(k,Z)→Dmot(k), sending a smooth scheme to its Berkovich motive, is an equivalence. A comparison for arbitrary nonclosed fields requires a separately specified descent versus hyperdescent convention and is not asserted here.
hypotheses: k is algebraically closed.
The comparison uses the integral étale category of BM.10.
proofSteps: Check the smooth-scheme functor satisfies étale descent, A¹-invariance and G_m-stability and hence factors through the universal category.

Compare the rational and prime-to-characteristic completed maps on compact dualizable smooth-projective generators using the two mapping-formula targets. Characteristic-p torsion vanishes on both sides. Arithmetic reconstruction gives full faithfulness; the discrete generation theorem gives essential surjectivity.

sources.locator: §11, Remark 11.2 and Theorem 11.1, pp. 57–58; §1, Proposition 1.13, p. 7
sources.match: Agreement on generators and their mapping spectra establishes the enhanced equivalence.

acceptance: Require the comparison to identify Tate objects and smooth-scheme generators, not merely produce an abstract categorical equivalence.

nodes.title: Motivic nearby cycles
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, C a completed algebraic closure of k((T)) with |T|=1/2, and f:Marc(C)→Marc(k). Choose a topologically nilpotent unit π and compatible roots π^(1/n) for n prime to the residue-characteristic exponent p. With g:tilde G_m→Marc(k) the inverse prime-to-p power tower, identify f_*Z≃g_*Z. Define Ψ:Dmot(C)≃Mod_{f_*Z}(Dmot(k))→Dmot(k) by extension of scalars along g_*Z→Z induced by the unit section.
hypotheses: This construction uses the chosen roots, not just the abstract residue field.
In characteristic zero p=1, so every positive integer is prime to p.
proofSteps: Good-reduction generators and Barr–Beck identify Dmot(C) with modules over f_*Z. Annulus continuity identifies that algebra with g_*Z; both have unit and cofiber Q(−1)[−1].
The compatible roots give the comparison to the tower and its augmentation at 1. Use module extension of scalars to define Ψ coherently as a symmetric monoidal colimit-preserving functor.

sources.match: Nearby cycles is an augmented-algebra base change depending on roots.

acceptance: Track the direction of the algebra augmentation and its scalar-extension functor.

The chosen section identifies its value with the underlying monodromy object.

nodes.title: Descendability of nearby cycles
nodes.statement: The augmentation f_*Z→Z defining Ψ is descendable. Consequently Ψ is conservative.
hypotheses: Use thick tensor-ideal generation in the module category, not solely convergence of an unbounded Amitsur limit.
proofSteps: The fibre of g_*Z→Z is Q(−1)[−1]; its g_*Z-module action factors through Z, as follows after rationalization from the free E-infinity algebra on Q(−1)[−1].
The resulting two-step filtration by inflated Z-modules puts the algebra in the thick tensor ideal generated by Z. Apply the imported descendability theorem.

sources.match: The two-step augmented-algebra filtration proves descendability.

acceptance: Check the module-action factorization as well as the underlying cofiber computation.

nodes.title: Residue-field motivic Galois stack
nodes.statement: Fix k=an algebraic closure of F_p. Define MG_k over Z[1/p] by a line L and compatible derived isomorphisms L⊗^L Z/n≃μ_n(k)⊗Z R for every n prime to p. Equivalently MG_k≃B G_m^rat, where the group G_m^rat has coordinate ring Q[t,t⁻¹]×_Q Z[1/p], where the first map to Q evaluates t at 1. Dqc(MG_k) is compactly generated by L^n for n∈Z.
hypotheses: The fibre product is a fibre product of rings over Q with Z[1/p]→Q; it is not their direct product.
Compatibility includes the transition maps between the different n.
proofSteps: Construct the line-with-Kummer-trivializations moduli functor using the AS.1 derived quasi-coherent stack machinery and identify it with the displayed group classifying stack.
Check its fibres: over F_ℓ for ℓ≠p the stack is a point; over Q it is BG_m. Pushforward preserves colimits and the powers of the line are compact generators, checked on these arithmetic fibres.

sources.match: The residue-field Tate category is modeled by a line with all compatible finite-coefficient trivializations.

acceptance: Do not omit the fibre-product gluing at the identity.

api.name: mg_line
api.statement: The tautological line has the specified coherent reductions for all prime-to-p n.

api.name: mg_arithmetic_fibres
api.statement: The rational fibre is BG_m and every finite prime-to-p fibre is a point.

api.name: mg_line_generators
api.statement: All integer powers of L are compact dualizable generators of Dqc(MG_k).

tests.name: rational_weights
tests.statement: Rationally the line powers are distinct G_m characters.

tests.name: finite_fibre
tests.statement: Modulo ℓ≠p the line is the constant μ_ℓ(k)-line and the category is D(F_ℓ).

tests.name: bad_prime
tests.statement: The stack is over Z[1/p], so its characteristic-p fibre is empty; it must not introduce a p-torsion Tate sector.

uses.how: Supplies the explicit special-fibre mixed Tate category.
It is the base of the value-group gerbe.

nodes.title: Mixed Tate categories and motivic t-structures
nodes.statement: For k=F_pbar and C as in nearby cycles, Dqc(MG_k)≃DMT(k), taking L to Z(1). Also DMT(C)⊗_{DMT(k)}Dmot(k)≃Dmot(C). The t-structures on DMT(k) and DMT(C) generated connectively by all Tate twists make Ψ conservative and t-exact.
hypotheses: The t-structure claim concerns the mixed Tate subcategories, not an unconditional motivic t-structure on all Dmot(k).
proofSteps: Import Quillen finite-field K-theory and filtered continuity to obtain K(F_pbar)_Q=Q[0]. Compare maps between powers of L and Tate twists rationally and modulo n to prove full faithfulness and identify the mixed Tate image.

The algebra f_*Z lies in DMT(k), so module base change gives the tensor-product identity. Cover MG_k by Spec Z[1/p]; the augmentation of the free E-infinity algebra on Q[−1] is coconnectively faithfully flat, proving t-exactness together with descendability.

sources.match: Finite-field K-theory makes the Tate category explicit and the module algebra descends to it.

acceptance: Check that maps between different rational Tate weights vanish.
Do not claim this describes all motives over F_pbar absolutely.

nodes.title: Valued-field motivic Galois gerbe
nodes.statement: For k=F_pbar and C the completed algebraic closure of k((T)), define MG_C over MG_k by adjoining a derived map (C×/(1+C<1))[−1]→L whose reductions modulo every n prime to p are the fixed Kummer identifications. Equivalently classify extensions L→Ltilde→(C×/(1+C<1))⊗R with the prescribed restriction to reduced integral units. The map h:MG_C→MG_k is a gerbe banded by Hom(Q,L), with h_*O having O in degree 0 and L∨⊗Q in degree 1.
hypotheses: The value group C×/O_C× is identified with Q using the norm normalization.
The extension restriction to O_C×/(1+C<1) is the canonical L→L⊗Q→L⊗Q/Z[1/p] triangle.
proofSteps: Construct the extension moduli with its derived finite-coefficient compatibilities. Quotienting reduced units by integral reduced units gives the value-group Q and identifies the band.
Compute the quasi-coherent cohomology of this affine unipotent band using its rational additive-group model; preserve the extension class, not only the two cohomology groups.

sources.locator: §11, definition of MG_C and ensuing computation, pp. 60–61
sources.match: The gerbe retains both Kummer torsion data and the rational value group.

acceptance: Specify the derived extension and all modulus compatibilities.

api.name: mgc_extension
api.statement: Its R-points are the displayed extensions with compatible integral-unit restriction.

api.name: mgc_band
api.statement: The relative gerbe band is Hom(Q,L), with the specified value-group normalization.

api.name: mgc_roots_section
api.statement: Compatible roots of π give a section h by splitting reduced units into value-group and integral-unit parts.

tests.name: value_group
tests.statement: The quotient of reduced units by reduced integral units is Q, not Z.

tests.name: finite_coefficients
tests.statement: Modulo n prime to p the gerbe retains the prescribed Kummer identifications; a bare rational gerbe is insufficient.

tests.name: chosen_split
tests.statement: A compatible root system yields a neutral gerbe. Its section is choice-dependent, even though the gerbe itself is defined without choosing it.

uses.how: The augmented E-infinity algebra h_*O is compared with f_*Z.
Its band representations give the locally nilpotent operator.

nodes.title: Galois-stack description of valued motives
nodes.statement: Dqc(MG_C)≃DMT(C), and Dmot(C)≃Dmot(k)⊗_{Dqc(MG_k)}Dqc(MG_C), for k=F_pbar and C as above.
hypotheses: The equivalences preserve the natural Dqc(MG_k)-linear symmetric monoidal structures.
proofSteps: Construct the map h_*O→f_*Z from the reduced-unit Tate class. Both have the same unit and rational degree-one summand. Identify the induced degree-one map with the identity of the normalized value group Q, not just an unspecified nonzero scalar.
Use the module descriptions on both sides and the residue Tate model to obtain the first equivalence. Apply module-category base change for the full-motive identity.

sources.match: The value-group computation identifies the actual algebra and hence the full relative category.

acceptance: An equality of the underlying two-term complexes without algebra compatibility is insufficient.

nodes.title: Locally nilpotent motivic monodromy pairs
nodes.statement: Over Dmot(k), define the monodromy-pair category as representations of the neutral affine unipotent band Hom(Q,Z(1)) obtained from a chosen section of MG_C→MG_k. Use its coalgebra/comodule model to specify all coherent structure. Under the characteristic-zero additive-group representation correspondence, this is an object A with a locally nilpotent operator N:A→A⊗Q(−1); local nilpotence means an exhaustive filtered union of subrepresentations on which a finite iterate of N vanishes, interpreted in the comodule category.
hypotheses: k=F_pbar in the explicit Galois-stack model.
The operator has rational negative Tate twist; it is not a general arbitrary endomorphism.
The comodule formulation fixes the derived coherence; vanishing solely on cohomology is not the definition.
proofSteps: Neutralize the gerbe using compatible roots and identify its quasi-coherent category with representations of its band.

Use the AS.1 affine-group/comodule construction and the characteristic-zero additive-group finite-stage correspondence, requested explicitly there, to identify representations with locally nilpotent twisted operators. Morphisms are coherent equivariant maps, hence commute with N under this correspondence.

sources.match: Neutralizing the value-group gerbe turns its representations into locally nilpotent monodromy.

acceptance: Keep the comodule model as the precise category definition until the derived operator equivalence is established by the AS.1 request.

api.name: monodromy_forget
api.statement: The underlying-object functor forgets the band coaction and retains the operator in its twisted form.

api.name: monodromy_morphisms
api.statement: Morphisms are equivariant maps, with the required higher coherence.

api.name: monodromy_tensor
api.statement: Tensor product has N_{A⊗B}=N_A⊗1+1⊗N_B and compatible twists.

tests.statement: Every A with trivial band action gives (A,0).

tests.name: rank_two_nilpotent

tests.name: nonnilpotent_excluded

Checks nontrivial unipotent as well as trivial monodromy.

nodes.title: Nearby cycles and monodromy equivalence
nodes.statement: For k=F_pbar and C the completed algebraic closure of k((T)), compatible prime-to-p roots of π give a symmetric monoidal equivalence Dmot(C)≃{(A,N):A∈Dmot(k), N:A→A⊗Q(−1) locally nilpotent}. Ψ corresponds to forgetting N. With rational coefficients the choice of π alone suffices.
hypotheses: Use the monodromy-pair category’s coherent comodule convention.

The explicit proof is stated over F_pbar. Extension to other residue fields requires the positive-characteristic base-change argument following Proposition 11.4, rather than dropping this specialization silently.
proofSteps: The compatible roots give a section of the value-group gerbe. Combine its neutral representation description with the Galois-stack equivalence and relative tensor-product identity.

Identify extension of scalars along the section with the underlying-object functor, so this equivalence realizes Ψ. Rationally the ordinary G_m tower already has the needed cohomology and a single π defines the augmentation.

sources.locator: §11, Corollary 11.10 and proof, pp. 61–62; §1, Theorem 1.14, p. 7
sources.match: A chosen gerbe section gives the relative monodromy description and the nearby-cycle forgetful functor.

acceptance: Check the Tate object has zero monodromy.
The theorem is a relative description over Dmot(k), not an absolute classification of all motives.

nodes.title: Normed arc-stacks and partially proper v-stacks
nodes.statement: On perfect analytic Banach F_p-algebras with a chosen norm, construct a*:vStack/N→arcStack and its fully faithful right adjoint b*:arcStack→vStack/N, where N is the canonical positive-real norm torsor. Explicitly (b*Y)(R,R+)=Y(R) and a*X is the sheafification of R↦X(R,R°). The essential image of b* is the partially proper v-stacks, characterized by independence of R+. For separated X, b*a*X is its canonical compactification.
hypotheses: All rings here are perfect analytic characteristic-p Banach rings.
Choose cardinal cutoffs before taking their compatible union.
proofSteps: At the ring level use the forgetful functor on Huber pairs and its adjoints R↦(R,R°) and R↦(R,integral closure of F_p+R°°). Verify finite-limit and cover compatibility on the opposite sites.
Obtain the sheaf adjunction and compute the unit/counit. Use the C4 canonical-compactification universal property to identify b*a* on separated v-stacks.

sources.match: The chosen norm requires the torsor base and the plus-insensitive image is partially proper.

acceptance: Track which functor is right adjoint and where the norm torsor enters.

api.name: arc_v_adjunction
api.statement: a* is left adjoint to b*, with b* fully faithful.

api.name: arc_v_image
api.statement: The essential image is exactly the plus-insensitive, partially proper v-stacks.

api.name: arc_v_compactification
api.statement: For separated X the comparison unit gives the canonical partially proper compactification.

tests.name: plus_independence
tests.statement: b*Y has equal values on (R,R+) and (R,R°).

tests.name: norm_base
tests.statement: Keeping a chosen norm gives vStack/N; it does not identify this category with all vStack without changing the test category.

tests.name: compactification
tests.statement: An already partially proper separated X is unchanged by b*a*, while a non-partially-proper separated X is replaced by its envelope.

uses.how: Provides the map from a v-stack to its Berkovich arc version.
Allows compact relative domains to be compared with quasicompact smooth diamond domains.

nodes.title: Norm-free Tate arc-stack comparison
nodes.statement: Use perfectoid Tate F_p-algebras without a chosen norm to define arcStack′ and functors a′*:vStack→arcStack′, b′*:arcStack′→vStack. Equivalently use Huber pairs with the topology generated by surjectivity on rank-one points. In this topology Spa(R,R°)→Spa(R,R+) is a cover, so the choice of plus subring disappears after sheafification.
hypotheses: This is a variant of the fixed-norm site, not an unannounced change to BM.0.
A norm on a fixed base recovers the earlier relative theory.
proofSteps: Choose norms locally on a fixed Tate base and use independence of compatible norms to glue the motivic categories.
Compare rank-one covers with the plus-forgetting sheafification, then construct the two functors exactly as in the normed comparison.

sources.locator: §12, discussion after Corollary 12.2 and before Proposition 12.3, p. 63
sources.match: The Tate variant removes the norm-torsor base while retaining the stronger rank-one topology.

acceptance: Prove the restriction to a normed base agrees with the original motivic category.

api.statement: The topology is tested by rank-one surjectivity on the Huber-pair test category.

api.name: normfree_plus_cover
api.statement: Spa(R,R°)→Spa(R,R+) is a cover.

api.statement: After choosing a norm on a base, the relative category agrees with the fixed-norm construction.

tests.statement: For R+=R° the plus-cover is the identity.

tests.name: smaller_plus
tests.statement: Replacing R+ by a smaller allowed integral subring changes the adic test space but not its arc-sheafification.

tests.name: higher_rank
tests.statement: The topology ignores additional higher-rank points for covering surjectivity; it is not simply the v-topology with another name.

uses.how: Its plus-forgetting property identifies the essential image of torsion pullback.
Places the two coefficient categories over a spatial diamond.

nodes.title: Torsion motives as overconvergent étale sheaves
nodes.statement: For a small characteristic-p v-stack X, let Y=a′*X and n prime to p. There is a fully faithful embedding Dmot(Y,Z/n)≃Det(Y,Z/n)→Det(X,Z/n). Its essential image consists of the overconvergent objects: the stalk at any higher-rank geometric point Spa(C,C+) agrees with that at its generic rank-one point Spa(C,O_C). The embedding respects pullback, tensor and proper finite-cohomological-dimension pushforward.
hypotheses: Det is the enhanced left-completed étale category supplied by DiamondEtaleCohomology.
The stalk condition uses the natural specialization map, not an abstract equality of groups.
proofSteps: Reduce by descent to strictly totally disconnected X. Use the C0/C2 comparison with sheaves on π₀X and its overconvergent essential-image characterization.
Pass from bounded-below to unbounded using the strict-base Postnikov computation. Check the three functor compatibilities on this basis and descend.

sources.match: Prime-to-p torsion motives retain exactly the plus-independent, overconvergent étale information.

acceptance: All these statements use n prime to p; no p-torsion diamond equivalence is inferred.
The higher-rank specialization map must be invertible, excluding a sheaf with different generic and higher-rank stalks.

nodes.title: Spatial-diamond categorical retract
nodes.statement: If X is a spatial diamond of finite cohomological dimension and n is prime to p, the preceding full inclusion Det(Y,Z/n)→Det(X,Z/n), Y=a′*X, has a colimit-preserving right adjoint. Det(X,Z/n) is compactly generated. Thus Det(Y,Z/n) is a retract of a compactly generated presentable category; compact generation of Det(Y,Z/n) itself is not asserted.
hypotheses: Use the compact-generation hypotheses and cohomological bounds from C9.
proofSteps: A generating compact map Zmot[U]→Zmot[V] for a strict domain inclusion becomes a map factoring through the homology of a quasicompact smooth diamond W/X. This is compact in Det(X,Z/n).
Hence the full inclusion preserves compact morphisms; the E5 adjoint criterion makes its right adjoint colimit-preserving. Import C9 compact generation to obtain the retract.

sources.match: Compact-morphism preservation identifies the motivic category as a categorical retract.

acceptance: Do not upgrade a retract of a compactly generated category to a compactly generated category without an additional theorem.

requests.need: Enhanced space-valued sheaves and derived sheaves on cardinal-cutoff sites, hypersheafification, slices, coherent pullback and descent of adjoints. Give the actual enhanced category and change-of-cutoff comparison; ordinary triangulated sheaf cohomology alone is insufficient.

The general Mondal–Reinecke theorem that the hypercomplete infinity-topos of a replete ordinary topos is Postnikov complete; also the finite-covering-dimension Postnikov criterion for sheaves on compact Hausdorff spaces, derived inverse-limit/completion and arithmetic reconstruction for the mapping spectra used here. The existing abelian-derived repleteness and locally weakly contractible space statements alone do not supply the first assertion.

The nonstable compact-assembly criterion for seminormed rings used in Proposition 2.9; the presentable monoidal Verdier quotient for a localizing tensor ideal; spectral ball localization and E-infinity arithmetic fracture. These are additions to the precise existing stable compact-assembly and small Verdier-quotient nodes, which are cited separately.

Free animated commutative monoids and their group completions, augmentation-ideal filtration with connectivity convergence, and the Breen–Deligne group-completion resolution in the exact form cited by Scholze Proposition 8.4 (Aoki Theorem 4.4). Supply primary-source verification of that general resolution.

Apply no new motivic definitions here: export Mann’s six-functor construction principle, the extension theorem Scholze 5.19 = Heyer–Mann 3.4.11, coherent base-change/projection and cohomological étaleness/smoothness criteria. BM.8 verifies these axioms for Banach motives.

Derived quasi-coherent categories and tensor descent for the algebraic stacks MG_k and MG_C; affine-group comodule categories; identify representations of Hom(Q,L) with coherent locally nilpotent L-dual-rational-twisted operators, including unbounded derived objects. This operator/comodule equivalence must be proved, not inferred just on cohomology.

Connective ring K-theory as the functorial E-infinity group completion of finite projective modules, enhanced to connective spectra and multiplicative for tensor product; the existing plus-space component description is a partial input, not an infinite-loop product splitting.

Suslin excision for a Tor-unital nonunital ideal I, with K(I)=fib(K(Z⊕I)→K(Z)) independent of unitization and its map to ambient K(A). Also the relative/truncating KH model for arbitrary idempotent ideals and A¹ localization needed to define the root-free KH-cofiber. Neither unrestricted K-excision nor automatic Tor-unitality of every ideal is allowed.

Functorial multiplicative Adams operations on rational connective ring K-theory for the abstract rings in the Banach site and compatibility with line bundles, supported completion and the codimension-one weight shift. Existing regular-noetherian-scheme operations supply only that narrower range; the E-infinity/all-ring extension must be explicit.
Quillen’s finite-field K calculation and compatibility with inclusions, followed by filtered continuity to K(F_pbar)_Q=Q[0]. Only the latter consequence is used for the residue Tate category.

Prime-to-residue-characteristic K-rigidity for the henselian pairs entering the field-cofiber comparison, with the actual maps and Bocksteins. The full geometric Gabber–Suslin field-extension assertion remains in the routed-ownership gap.

Verify and supply K(O_C)^∧p≃K(C)^∧p for algebraically closed complete C and K(k)^∧p≃Z_p for perfect characteristic-p fields, in the exact form cited as Hesselholt–Nikolaus Lemma 1.3.7 and Kratzer Corollary 5.5 in Scholze Corollary 8.10. This p-completed K statement is beyond a bare THH calculation and needs the trace/K comparison. Preserve p=2 as well.

Import the represented Pic⁰/Jacobian and functorial line-bundle moduli on a smooth proper geometrically connected curve. The new marked-trivialization torus torsor is constructed in BM.4; do not duplicate the ordinary Jacobian.

Multiplication by every positive integer is surjective on points of an abelian variety over an algebraically closed field, including inseparable multiplication in its characteristic. Combine with the torus case to prove the new semiabelian divisibility.

Rational sections/divisors on smooth projective curves and their approximation/Riemann–Roch API. The analytic extension to controlling entire boundary discs is requested from TB.0 rather than attributed to algebraic point interpolation alone.

The field-case de Jong alteration and normal-crossing compactification theorem with its dominance, generic-finiteness and base-extension hypotheses, and the proper-hypercover descent route when the degree is not invertible. Rational trace splitting may be used only rationally.
Perfectoid strict bases and the almost structure-sheaf localization on closed subsets needed by torsion almost modules. Retain the actual plus subrings and complete idempotent algebra structures.
Perfectoid arc/v-basis descent and tilting of the corresponding sites, with cutoff and cover conditions. The Banach arc-site itself is constructed here and is not identified with the scheme arc-site.
Small v-stacks and cardinal-cutoff geometry, their fibre products and geometric-point descriptions for the v/arc comparison.
Perfectoid Huber-pair and analytic diamond interface, the plus-subring and norm-free Tate presentations and site comparisons used by BM.12.
